docs.title: neuPod
docs.text:
neuPod is a drop-in replacement logic board for the Apple iPod Classic 6G (A1238). It reuses the original shell, click wheel and (optionally) screen, and adds Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, microSD storage and USB-C. The firmware is written from scratch.

Two compute platforms are evaluated side by side from one source tree:

  • Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W / RP2350 — primary, Phase 1 testbed in progress
  • ESP32-S3 — comparison

docs.title: Audio output (I2S, test signals, WAV, FLAC, MP3, ALAC)
docs.text: Phase 1 sound comes out of the Pimoroni Pico Audio Pack ("the Audio Pack DAC") over I2S, driven by the PIO and DMA from the bare-metal audio core (ADR-0011, Runtime). The audio policy is ADR-0003: decode once to a 32-bit mixer, no resampling; the sink is re-clocked per file instead.

docs.title: Pins
docs.text:
Signal GPIO Notes I2S DATA GP9 PIO0 out pin I2S BCK GP10 PIO0 side-set bit 0 I2S LRCK GP11 PIO0 side-set bit 1 (BCK and LRCK must be consecutive) Mute / amp enable GP22 plain GPIO, driven by core 1 (and by core 0 at boot and in the fatal-error path)

The Audio Pack is a TI PCM5100A DAC with a PAM8908 headphone amp behind the "phones" jack (low/high gain switch); "line out" is the DAC output directly. Try both jacks.

No MCLK: the PCM5100A runs its internal PLL from BCK, which must be 32, 48 or 64 × fs with a 50 % LRCK. Our 32-bit slots give 64 fs. SCK is tied low on the Pack; the format pin is hardwired to standard I2S (one-BCK delay), which is what neupod_i2s.pio produces.

docs.title: Resource allocation
docs.text:
Resource Used by Notes PIO0, 1 state machine, 8 instructions I2S transmitter (platforms/rp2350/hal/neupod_i2s.pio) claimed with pio_claim_unused_sm, program added and removed at open/close. pio1 = SD (carlk3), pio2 = CYW43 + click wheel 2 DMA channels (claimed dynamically) ping-pong, chained A to B to A, 512 words each (256 stereo frames) high bus priority; read pointer wraps inside its 2 KB buffer (ring), so a late restart replays the old block instead of reading past the buffer DMA_IRQ_1, enabled on core 1 block-complete interrupt, refills the finished buffer DMA_IRQ_0 stays with the SD library on core 0 2 x 2 KB DMA buffers, 32 KB PCM ring, 32 KB data ring RAM PCM ring size is NEUPOD_PCM_RING_FRAMES in app/os/memory_budget.h; data ring in audio_shared.c Hot path in RAM dma_isr, on_block, audio_apply_gain, the ring functions, hal_audio_write, hal_audio_mute NEUPOD_RAM_FUNC / __not_in_flash_func

The sink is chosen at build time: scripts/build.sh rp2350 -- -DNEUPOD_AUDIO_SINK=i2s (default) or null (the old discard-on-a-clock sink, touches no pins). The host build uses SDL for audible output when SDL2 and an audio device exist (NEUPOD_HOST_AUDIO=0 forces silence), otherwise it is the null sink.

On the Innioasis Y2 the wired sink is the headphone jack's CS43131 DAC (Y2, Audio): the audio core is unchanged (same 32-bit blocks, same software volume and ramps); the HAL converts to 16 bit (TPDF dither whenever the volume or a deeper source leaves bits below the 16th), queues the blocks in a ring, and a writer thread paces the whole player on the DAC's clock. 44.1 kHz only, with the null sink as the fallback when no headphones are plugged in. hal_audio_wired_attached() tells the audio route whether anything is on the jack (always true on the other platforms): headphones pulled out while playing pause the player with a "Headphones unplugged" banner. The Y2's internal speaker and Line out use the same sink: hal_audio_set_speaker() / hal_audio_set_line_out() carry the route's decision (Settings > Speaker, Settings > Line out, Audio output Auto / Wired / Bluetooth / Speaker) to the HAL, hal_audio_headphones_in() and hal_audio_speaker_available() / hal_audio_line_out_available() report the hardware; the other platforms answer no. The amplifier-off-first rules, the volume caps (speaker 9, jack 11, Line out 15) and the allow-lists are in Y2. Line out locks the software volume at 0 dB (player_volume_set_locked()).

docs.title: Interrupt flow
docs.text:
1. Start: both buffers hold silence; DMA channel A is started, the PIO is enabled.
  2. When a channel finishes it chains to the other one and raises DMA_IRQ_1.
  3. The handler acknowledges, then for the finished buffer calls the block callback (on_block in app/audio/audio_core.c), which reads 256 frames from the PCM ring, applies volume, writes them into the buffer through hal_audio_write. The handler re-arms that channel's count.
  4. Ring empty: that block is silence and underruns counts it. If the interrupt runs so late that both buffers finished, dma_underruns (sink_missed) counts it and the old block is replayed once. If the late interrupt finds the other buffer's channel already restarted, the finished sibling is re-armed with its old block (never left at a zero count, which would end the ping-pong).
  5. 32 starved blocks in a row (186 ms) while playing: playback stops, the output is muted and the event STORM is logged.

docs.title: Sink restart (re-clock on a sample-rate change)
docs.text:
Close and hal_audio_force_mute() stop the sink in a fixed order, registers only and with bounded waits: mute pin; (close only) DMA interrupt off; clear the EN bit of both channels through the non-triggering AL1_CTRL alias (so the chain cannot re-trigger the sibling, RP2350-E5); abort both and wait for CHAN_ABORT and BUSY to clear; disable their INTE1 bits and acknowledge INTS1; disable the state machine, clear its FIFOs, restart it and its clock divider, clear its FDEBUG flags. It is safe to call twice or with nothing open. Open starts from the same clean state (the claimed channels are quiesced, pio_sm_init), configures both channels, clears INTS1 and the pending NVIC bit, enables the interrupt, then starts channel A and enables the state machine. Before this fix a rate switch could leave channel A armed and busy while the PIO requested data and nothing moved (audio core stalled). The dma_underruns=2 seen once per reopen is gone too; the likely explanation is the two stale chained channels completing after the unwaited abort (consistent with the counter now reading 0, not proven). An abort that has not completed within the spin bound (about 2 ms) is counted (g_abort_timeouts, readable over SWD) and makes open return HAL_EBUSY rather than configure a running channel. In the late-interrupt path, if both channels are found idle after re-arming the sibling, the sibling is restarted (the ping-pong had stopped).

Bench, 3 Nov 2026 (Pico 2 W): 12 ALAC 44.1 ↔ 96 kHz switches while playing, a switch from a paused 96 kHz stream and an ALAC 96 kHz → WAV 44.1 kHz switch: no stall, dma_underruns=0 after every reopen (was 2 every time).

docs.title: Clocking and rate accuracy
docs.text:
The PIO runs at 128 x Fs: two PIO cycles per BCK, 64 BCK per frame (32-bit slots). The divider comes from clk_sys = 125 MHz in 1/256 steps (16.8 fixed point), rounded to nearest.

Fs divider achieved Fs error BCK PIO cycle 44.1 kHz 22 + 37/256 44099.488 Hz -11.6 ppm 2.8224 MHz 177 ns 48 kHz 20 + 88/256 48003.072 Hz +64 ppm 3.0722 MHz 163 ns 88.2 kHz 11 + 18/256 88214.538 Hz +165 ppm 5.6457 MHz 89 ns 96 kHz 10 + 44/256 96006.144 Hz +64 ppm 6.1444 MHz 81 ns

The monitor line audio sink: prints the actual rate and divider read back from the hardware setup. Consequences:

  • The DAC slaves to BCK, so a rate error is not a sync problem; it only changes pitch and duration, by at most 165 ppm (0.29 cent; a 4-minute track is 40 ms shorter or longer). Not audible.
  • The fractional divider dithers each PIO cycle between 22 and 23 system clocks (and so on), so a BCK edge moves by at most one system clock, 8 ns, around its ideal place: 2 % of a 354 ns BCK period at 44.1 kHz, 5 % at 96 kHz. A DAC that regenerates its clock with a PLL (as no-MCLK DACs do) filters this. Not measured on the board; an oscilloscope on GP10 would show it.
  • 88.2 and 96 kHz are generated by the same code and accepted by the WAV player, but were not run on hardware.

docs.title: Mute line (GP22)
docs.text:
• GP22 drives the PCM5100A's XSMT pin (TSSOP-20 pin 17), active LOW: low = soft-muted, high = playing (design response, 3 Nov 2026, from the Pack schematic; confirmed on the bench the same day). The build default NEUPOD_AUDIO_UNMUTE_LEVEL=1 is correct.
  • The DAC also auto-mutes on a clock error: BCK and LRCK must be running continuously, and its PLL locked, before XSMT goes high.
  • Current behaviour (as built): muted from boot (hal_system_init), at sink open and close, on stop, on an underrun storm and in the fatal-error path (hal_panic → hal_audio_force_mute(), which also aborts the DMA and stops the PIO). The audio core opens XSMT one block before a fade-in and closes it after two silent blocks (app/audio/audio_core.c), and hal_audio_close() stops the I2S clocks between streams. So XSMT toggles with every start/stop. The stream is opened at boot and its clocks keep running, so in practice XSMT rises long after the PLL has locked.
  • Bench, 3 Nov 2026: works. 1 kHz test tone heard on the "line out" jack (DAC direct, no PAM8908) at -30 dB. The earlier silence was wiring: the GP9 (DATA) and GP22 (XSMT) jumpers were on the wrong Pico pins. Register read-back over SWD (SIO_IN / IO_BANK0 STATUS) showed both pins driven correctly while the Pack end read 0 V, which is how it was found.
  • Design recommendation (optional, not built): raise XSMT once after the clocks have settled and leave it high, doing start/stop/pause with the gain ramp only; XSMT low only for force-mute (panic, storm) and sink close. Not needed for function on the testbed; it reduces DAC soft-mute ramps at track boundaries.

docs.title: Volume safety
docs.text:
• Volume is attenuation in whole dB, applied in the 32-bit domain. Start-up level is -30 dB and is sent to the audio core before anything can play; the audio core also boots at -30 dB by itself. The volume is saved on the card (settings store, Bluetooth) together with the output path, and restored at boot by the Volume restore policy: the saved level on the same known path, otherwise capped at -30 dB. Nothing reports the output path yet, so today every restore is capped at -30 dB, as before.
  • The UI steps 2 dB per wheel click. The engine never applies gain above 0 dB, and a build-time hard cap (NEUPOD_AUDIO_VOLUME_CAP_DB, default 0, meaning full scale allowed) sets the loudest level; raise it for a headphone-safe build. At 80 dB or more the output is silent.
  • The test tone is -20 dBFS; with the default volume it reaches the DAC at -50 dBFS peak. The Test tone screen prints that figure. Leaving the Test tone screen stops the sound.
  • Volume changes, pause, resume, start and stop are ramped linearly across one 5.8 ms block (no clicks).

docs.title: Bit-perfect note
docs.text: PCM files are converted to 32 bits exactly (16-bit << 16, 24-bit << 8, 32-bit as is; mono duplicated to both channels), with no dither and no resampling. At 0 dB volume the samples then go to the DAC unchanged (verified by the unit tests; the gain stage is skipped). Only 0 dB is bit-perfect: any other setting multiplies the samples. The first and last block of a start/stop/pause are ramped even at 0 dB. The DAC itself and its analogue stage are not "bit-perfect" in any measurable sense; the claim is about the digital path. The Audio Pack DAC takes 32-bit slots; how many of the bits it uses is the DAC's business.

docs.title: Test signals and WAV
docs.text:
Source What Notes 1 kHz tone sine, -20 dBFS peak, both channels phase accumulator, 1024-point table with linear interpolation (worst error about -104 dBFS) L/R ident 400 Hz on the left only for 1 s, then 1600 Hz on the right only for 1 s, repeating (low = left, high = right) switches at a zero crossing; if you hear it in the wrong ear the channel order is swapped (slot order is left first) Scale C4 D4 E4 F4 G4 A4 B4 C5, then B4 down to C4, 300 ms per note, 10 ms raised-cosine attack and release, 600 ms rest, loops until stopped equal temperament, A4 = 440 Hz; frequencies rounded to a millihertz, phase step exact to 2^-32 WAV integer PCM 16/24/32-bit, mono or stereo, 44.1/48/88.2/96 kHz RIFF parser walks the chunks (LIST and other chunks before data, odd sizes, extensible PCM); float, 8-bit, other rates and RF64 are rejected with a message

A different sample rate re-clocks the sink (close and reopen, a few ms) with no resampling. The tones run at the sink's current rate (44.1 kHz after boot, or the last file's rate). The storage task reads the card in 2 KB steps into a 32 KB ring (85 ms at 32-bit stereo 48 kHz). End of file raises an end-of-track event after the last sample has played, then the output ramps down and mutes.

docs.title: Codecs: FLAC, MP3, ALAC (and WAV)
docs.text:
Format Decoder Licence Runs on Output FLAC (16/20/24/32-bit, mono/stereo, 44.1/48/88.2/96 kHz) dr_flac (single header, app/third_party/dr_libs/) public domain / MIT-0 core 1 exact: the sample is shifted left-justified into 32 bits MP3 (MPEG-1/2 Layer III, 44.1/48 kHz) dr_mp3 (contains minimp3) public domain / MIT-0 (minimp3 CC0) core 1 float, rounded to nearest and clipped to 32 bits ALAC in .m4a (16/20/24-bit; 32-bit rejected, mono/stereo, 44.1 to 96 kHz) Apple's ALAC decoder core (app/third_party/alac/) with a C wrapper (alac_dec.c) Apache-2.0 (see the repository's LICENSE.md: no NOTICE file upstream; the C port is marked as modified) core 1 exact AAC in .m4a none yet n/a n/a the player says "AAC not supported yet" WAV our own parser (wav.c), raw PCM passthrough MPL-2.0 conversion on core 1 exact

dr_wav is vendored with the others as requested but is not compiled: the WAV path has no codec in it, only a header parser that we already have and test, so dr_wav would add code without adding capability. More than 2 channels are rejected with a message, as are unsupported rates ("Unsupported sample rate"); mono is played on both sides.

docs.title: Where things run
docs.text:
• Core 0 (storage task) reads the file, parses the header and tags, and streams bytes through the 32 KB data ring:
    • FLAC: a synthesised 42-byte header (fLaC + one STREAMINFO block) followed by the audio frames, so the decoder never has to stream through the file's pictures and comments. Tags (Vorbis comments) are read here.
    • MP3: the compressed bytes from the first frame header on (ID3v2 skipped and parsed here; duration from the Xing/Info frame count, otherwise estimated from the file size, which can be far off for VBR files that lack one; shown with a ~).
    • M4A: the container is demuxed here (it needs random access to moov): app/audio/mp4.c reads stsd (the ALAC magic cookie), stsz, stsc, stco/co64, mdhd and the ilst tags, and sends each packet with a 4-byte big-endian length in front. The demuxer is codec independent so AAC can use it later.
    • Pictures: the tag readers do not load them. They record where each embedded picture is (audio_tags_t.art: file offset, length, kind JPEG / PNG / other, picture type) from the MP3 ID3v2 APIC / PIC frame, the FLAC PICTURE block and the MP4 covr item, reading only the few header bytes that say where the image starts and its first four bytes to tell JPEG from PNG: a 2 MB PNG costs the same few reads as a 2 KB one. A JPEG is preferred to a PNG, a front cover (type 3) to other types. Unsynchronised, compressed or encrypted ID3 frames cannot be streamed and are ignored. The art itself is decoded afterwards by the storage task (see UI).
  • Core 1 decodes. The main loop calls the decoder for up to two 256-frame blocks per pass while the PCM ring has room; the block interrupt is unchanged and still preempts it. Everything the decoders allocate comes from one static arena of 116 KB (codec.h), reset at every new stream: malloc is never called (the vendored allocation macros point at the arena), asserts are compiled out, and there is no stdio. tools/check_core1_closure.py (Python is required by the RP2350 build; ctest also runs the checker against a known-good and a known-bad fixture, so it is proven able to fail) runs after every RP2350 build and fails it if anything reachable from the audio core's entry points could reach the RTOS, stdio, the heap, blocking SDK calls or the panic path (it walks the call graph of the linked image, following branches and every function address found in literal pools; a function whose address is only ever computed would be missed, see the limits in the script's header); the audio_core_rules token scan still covers our own sources. Core 1's stack is now a 16 KB array of our own (minimp3 alone keeps about 10 KB of scratch on the stack).
  • Waiting for data: the decoder's read callback blocks until the bytes are there (core 0 refills at about 2 MB/s). While it waits it keeps handling commands: volume, pause and the end-of-stream marker immediately; anything that tears the stream down (stop, a new track, a tone) is parked, the read is abandoned and the command runs next, so nothing can deadlock. 32 starved blocks in a row still stops and mutes the output.
  • The first block of audio is not played until about 23 ms are buffered (and a stream is complete if it is shorter), so a slow start is silence rather than an underrun.
  • Seeking inside the decoder (the Now Playing seek is different, see "Seeking to a frame" below): forward seeks inside the decoder (including dr_flac's own) discard bytes; an absolute seek backwards sends core 0 a request (byte offset), core 0 repositions the file and acknowledges, core 1 then empties the data ring and acknowledges back, and only then does core 0 write again (stream_io.h; unit-tested with a real second thread).

docs.title: Gapless playback and the play queue
docs.text:
Decision record: ADR-0016. The queue is the playable files of the folder a track was chosen from, in Files order; the player (core 0) owns it. Gapless is on by default (Settings, "Gapless playback").

Handshake. Every stream core 0 starts or announces gets a sequence number; its description (audio_stream_desc_t) and its length in bytes live in g_audio_slot[seq & 1]. The data ring carries streams back to back.

  1. Hard start (audio_stream_start, command STREAM_START, a = sequence number): core 1 flushes both rings, re-clocks the sink if the rate differs, ramps, as before. It cancels any announcement.
  2. Once the current decoder is open (core 1 publishes g_audio_open_seq), the storage task asks the player which track follows, opens and parses it (the rate and channel count must match) and announces it: audio_stream_next() fills the other slot, sets g_audio_next_valid and sends STREAM_NEXT. Core 1 only remembers the number (it handles this command while waiting for data too).
  3. When the current track is completely in the ring, audio_stream_end() publishes its byte count in its slot and the announced track's bytes follow immediately. Core 1's byte source (sio_t.end) reads the ring first and the length second, so whenever it sees the next stream's bytes it also sees the boundary; reads never cross it, and the decoder sees the end of its stream there. Codecs that stop early because of trimming (see below) skip the rest of the stream up to the boundary.
  4. The decoder returns its last frame: core 1 looks at the command ring once more (an announcement sent just before the end is not missed), then, if the announcement is still valid (g_audio_next_valid re-read after copying the description), closes the decoder, opens the next one on the same sink, PCM ring and volume (the decoders' byte source g_sio is rebuilt for every stream, WAV included, so a WAV that hands over to a codec track never opens it on an unset source), and pushes the number of PCM frames written so far into a small boundary ring. The block interrupt counts the frames it serves; when they reach the boundary it reports END_OF_TRACK with value 1 and elapsed restarts. So the event fires in the block that carries the old track's last sample (within 256 frames), not when decoding ends. No mute change, no ramp.
  5. Nothing announced (last track, gapless off, other rate or channel count, unreadable file, a track too short to chain): the track ends as before (ring drains, ramp, END_OF_TRACK value 0) and the player starts the next one with a hard start.

Seeks: a decoder only seeks while it opens, when nothing can be announced yet. A seek request nevertheless withdraws an announcement and the end marker (core 0), and g_audio_next_valid makes a stale STREAM_NEXT harmless. Stop, skip or a new start clear g_audio_next_valid before anything reuses a slot; core 1 drops its pending note on stop. Only one handoff may be pending at a time. A different format is refused by core 1 too (error event, the track ends normally).

Encoder delay and padding. FLAC and WAV lengths are exact. MP3: with a LAME tag dr_mp3 drops delay + 529 frames at the start and padding - 529 at the end; the parser reports exactly the length it will deliver, and the codec layer does not trim again. Without a LAME tag nothing is trimmed (and a missing frame count gives an estimate, shown with ~). ALAC/M4A: the edit list (elst, one non-empty entry: media_time = priming, segment_duration = length) is preferred, else iTunSMPB (hex: priming, padding, original length). A trim that does not fit the media is ignored. The reported total_frames is the trimmed length. The test vectors: tools/gen_trim_vectors.py.

Host tests. gapless runs the real core-1 loop and the real core-0 stream controller against a fake sink with a real-time block clock and compares the sink's samples frame by frame with each track decoded on its own (WAV, FLAC, MP3, ALAC with an edit list; skip, stop, seek and rate change cases). play_queue covers the queue rules (including shuffle permutations, repeat, wrap re-shuffle) and player the mid-play toggles.

Shuffle and repeat (Settings > Shuffle / Repeat, saved; Now Playing shows small shuffle/loop icons, loop with a 1 for repeat-one): see the amendment in ADR-0016. UART reasons added: repeat, wrap (and gapless repeat, gapless wrap).

Bench, 3 Nov 2026 (Pico 2 W): 30-signals/gapless/ (3-part FLAC then 3-part LAME MP3, one queue): five (gapless) handoffs incl. FLAC → MP3, one END_OF_TRACK(1) per boundary, sink never re-clocked, mute line open throughout, 0 underruns. Next / Previous (restart when more than 3 s in, previous track within 3 s) / Next on the last track (queue end) correct; a skip while the successor was being announced leaves later joins gapless. Gapless Off: (auto) joins with the ramp, setting persists across a reboot. 44.1 → 48 kHz in 10-matrix/: (auto) with a re-clock, dma_underruns=0, 0 underruns.

docs.title: Resume (last track and position)
docs.text:
The player (core 0) remembers the folder track that was playing and where (app/runtime/resume.c, two settings items NPr0/NPr1: track path, folder entry index, 64-bit file size, position in PCM frames, playing or paused; the entry, not the shuffle slot, is saved). It is stored when the user pauses or resumes, when a track starts (also a gapless or repeat one) and on Stop (the place is kept). Under repeat-all or repeat-one the album never ends, so the record is never cleared; without repeat the end of the album clears it. These calls only change the RAM image (serialised by a small mutex, as the UI and the storage task both call them); the SD write is the settings store's own save on the storage task (write lock opened only inside that save, nothing on core 1).

There is no periodic update by default. The rule "no SD writes while audio plays" stands, and a mid-track update could only be written during playback: the write runs on the storage task that also refills the audio data ring, so a card that stalls for 100-250 ms for one write would underrun a high-rate stream (at 24-bit/96 kHz the rings hold only about 85-130 ms). So a power cut mid-track resumes at the last pause, resume, Stop or track start, not at the exact second. An opt-in build exception exists (RESUME_WRITE_WHILE_PLAYING 1, resume.h; default 0, unbenched): it adds a 30 s update (RESUME_PERIOD_MS) and writes it during playback only when the data ring plus the PCM ring hold at least 300 ms of audio (judged pessimistically as 32-bit stereo, so it rarely opens), times each such write, and turns itself off for the boot if one takes over 50 ms. There is no orderly-shutdown hook in the firmware yet (no power-off path); pausing before switching off stores the exact place.

At boot, right after the settings load, the storage task lists the saved folder (only if the UI has not listed anything yet: the listing buffer is shared), resume_plan() decides, and the player opens the track (in a queue built with the saved shuffle and repeat modes: under shuffle the order is new, the track is the saved one) paused at the saved frame (nothing is played until the user presses play): the file is there with the same size: that frame; same name but another size: the same track from the beginning; the file is gone: the playable entry at the saved queue position, from its beginning; the folder cannot be read, or holds nothing playable, or the track cannot be opened: the record is discarded.

Resume playing on power-up (Settings, NPra, u8, default Off; player_resume_autoplay()): Off keeps the behaviour above (always paused). On: the same restore, but when the saved record says it was playing (resume_state_t.playing) the track starts playing instead of being paused (player_resume_folder(..., play)); a record that says paused or stopped still restores paused. The setting is read after the settings load and the volume restore (same task, in that order), so auto-play uses the restored volume, including the -30 dB cap for an unknown or different output path. A track that cannot be opened is dropped quietly in both modes.

Seeking to a frame (track_feed_seek(), core 0 only; the one core-1 change is that the FLAC decoder honours skip_frames):

Codec Start position WAV exact frame (the byte) ALAC (M4A) exact frame: the packet is found with the sample tables (mp4_iter_seek: the stsc runs and one chunk, not every packet before it) and the decoder drops the frames before the target; trimming (edit list, iTunSMPB) stays exact FLAC exact frame if the file has a SEEKTABLE (nearest earlier seek point, the decoder drops the rest); without one the track starts at the beginning (position 0) MP3 nearest frame: from the Xing table of contents or the Fraunhofer VBRI table (VBR) or the byte proportion (CBR, within a frame; VBR roughly 1%; a file with no frame count at all uses an estimate from its first frame's bit rate), then a resync to a frame header confirmed by the one after it. The position that is then shown and saved is computed back from where the frame header really landed, so errors do not add up over repeated resumes. The first granule after the jump may be silent (bit reservoir) and the LAME end padding is no longer trimmed

tools/gen_seek_vector.py makes the FLAC vector with a seek table for the tests (tests/test_gapless.c, through the real core-1 loop).

Seek from Now Playing (player_seek(), UI-7): the same file is started again at the target frame, a hard start exactly like the boot resume, so core 1 sees an ordinary new stream and nothing new crosses between the cores. Consequences: a short mute (the ramp-down, the ring flush and the decoder opening; the audio core's underrun and storm counters are not involved); an announced gapless successor is withdrawn by the stop and the player's counters are re-based, and the stream controller announces it again for the restarted stream once its ring is full, so the handoff at the end of the track stays sample-exact (tests/test_gapless.c, seek during prefetch); paused stays paused (the restarted stream is paused before anything is fed). Only tracks whose track_info_t.seekable is set are offered it: WAV, ALAC, MP3 (UI-7: the scrub bar and the time show where an MP3 really landed, so a VBR file moves in jumps of up to about 1 % of the track), and FLAC with a SEEKTABLE and a known length (it is exact; without a table the only way would be decoding from the start; such a FLAC answers Seek not available). A target at or past the last frame is the end of the track: the queue advances as it does when a track plays out (repeat-one restarts it, the last track stops). Scrubbing applies one restart per rest of the wheel (0.35 s), not one per step. The player counts the start requests it has posted (the storage task answers each exactly once, in order) and applies only the answer to the last one, so a seek followed by another seek, Next or a seek to the end never shows the replaced start's track data; the answer to a replaced start that fails is ignored too. When a seek's restart is up, the new position is saved for resume once (RESUME_EVENT), not per scrub step.

docs.title: Memory and CPU
docs.text:
Value Arena 99 KB (101,376 bytes, CODEC_ARENA_BYTES). Measured high water: FLAC 4096-sample blocks 35 KB; MP3 57 to 68 KB; ALAC 16-bit 82,072 B, 24-bit 98,456 B. Computed worst cases (arena_worst_cases_fit): FLAC at the 8192-sample limit (4096 for 32-bit FLAC, which dr_flac stores at 8 bytes a sample) 72,128 B, MP3 56,984 B, ALAC 24-bit stereo 4096 frames 98,472 B. ALAC 24-bit is the binding case; the arena is that plus a 2 KB margin, rounded up to 1 KB Limits that follow FLAC blocks above 8192 samples (4096 for 32-bit FLAC) are rejected ("FLAC block size too large"); the synthesised header declares exactly that limit, so the decoder's sample buffer is allocated once at full size and a larger frame fails instead of growing the arena; ALAC packets of at most 16384 frames are accepted by the parser but only 4096-frame packets are guaranteed to fit; 32-bit ALAC is rejected on core 0 ("32-bit ALAC not supported") and again in alac_dec_init on core 1, because 4096-frame 32-bit stereo needs about 115 KB of arena Data ring 32 KB, 32-bit stereo 48 kHz is 85 ms PCM ring NEUPOD_PCM_RING_FRAMES = 4096 frames, 32 KB (app/os/memory_budget.h): 93 ms at 44.1 kHz, 43 ms at 96 kHz. The earlier 2048 frames (46 ms / 21 ms) underran 66 times in 30 s on ALAC 16/44.1 and about 2600 times on ALAC 24/96 RAM budget Arena 116 to 99 KB (-17 KB) funds the PCM ring 16 to 32 KB (+16 KB): net -1 KB. The ALAC hot paths in SRAM cost about 6.5 KB of .data (see below) Hot paths in SRAM ALAC alac_dec_decode, dyn_decomp, unpc_block, unmix16/24/32, copyPredictorTo24/32 (+Shift) and the BitBuffer readers run from RAM via NEUPOD_RAM_FUNC (app/third_party/alac/README.md) Measured RP2350 load of core 1 (bench, ALAC code in SRAM, ring 2048) ALAC 16/44.1: 30.2 % load, worst packet decode 27.9 ms (38.4 % and 57 ms with the code in flash), 0 underruns; ALAC 24/96: 71.7 % load, worst packet 30 ms; MP3 worst 37 ms. With the 4096-frame ring a 30 ms decode fits inside 43 ms at 96 kHz; bench 3 Nov 2026, ring 4096: ALAC 24/96 0 underruns over 60 s, 72.4 % load, worst packet 30.4 ms, lowest ring fill 1280 frames (13 ms spare), arena high water 98,456 of 101,376 B; FLAC 16/44.1 album (35 min) 0 underruns at 7 to 8 % load Host decode speed (i7-12700T, -O2, the test vectors, MD5 hashing included) FLAC 16/44.1: 547x real time; FLAC 24/96: 409x; MP3: 720x; ALAC 16/44.1: 322x; ALAC 24/48: 286x (NEUPOD_BENCH=1 test_codecs) Estimated RP2350 load of core 1 (not measured) FLAC 16/44.1 about 10 to 20 %, FLAC 24/96 about 15 to 35 %, MP3 about 10 to 25 %, ALAC 16/44.1 about 20 to 35 %, ALAC 24/48 about 25 to 40 %. Basis: about 2x the x86 cycles per sample at 125 MHz, before flash cache misses (the decoder code runs from flash). The vectors are noisy, so real music should be cheaper. Measure with the line below

The monitor prints, every 10 s, audio decoder: codec=... decode_us_per_256_frames avg/max=.../... load=..% of a core ... arena_high_water=.... The figure is the time the decoder spent per 256 output frames with the block interrupt's own time subtracted, its worst single call, and the average as a share of the 5.8 ms block period (at 44.1 kHz). The ALAC hot loops already run from RAM.

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text: FLAC Vorbis comments (TITLE, ARTIST, ALBUM, TRACKNUMBER), ID3v2.2/2.3/2.4 text frames (TIT2, TPE1, TALB, TRCK; ISO-8859-1, UTF-16 and UTF-8), and MP4 ilst (©nam, ©ART, ©alb, trkn) are parsed on core 0 and shown on Now Playing with the format badge (FLAC 24/96, MP3 320k or MP3 VBR ~192k, ALAC 16/44.1) and the elapsed and remaining time. The screen font has no accented letters, so those show as an empty box. Embedded art is not read yet.

docs.title: FLAC verify mode (check without listening)
docs.text: In Extras > Files, press Right on a .flac (Select plays it). The decoder runs flat out with no sound, hashes every decoded sample the way FLAC defines its checksum (each sample as ceil(bits/8) little-endian bytes, channels interleaved) and compares it with the MD5 in the file's STREAMINFO at the end of the file. Now Playing shows MD5 OK, MD5 MISMATCH or No MD5 stored in this file, and the UART prints verify: '<name>' MD5 OK. A mismatch means the data from the card or the decoder is wrong, so it tests the whole path from the card to the decoder. (An MD5 of all zeros means the encoder did not compute one.)

docs.title: Robustness
docs.text: Files are untrusted input. The header parsers bound every length and walk (box sizes are compared without wrapping, a box budget of 20,000, vendor and comment lengths checked, text conversion never writes past its buffer); ALAC rejects a partial-frame sample count above its frame length (the original decoder trusted it); an MP4 packet outside the file or larger than the decoder's frame buffer ends the stream; a decode that ends short of the announced length is an error ("File is truncated or damaged"), so a damaged FLAC can never report MD5 OK or Finished; and a codec error makes core 0 stop reading the card. Once a command has interrupted the decoder's wait, every further read fails until the engine has handled it. Core 1's stack has a hardware limit (MSPLIM) 256 bytes above its bottom, so an overflow faults instead of corrupting RAM. The tests truncate every vector at each early byte and at 40 further points and flip random bits (fixed seed) in all of FLAC, MP3 and M4A; -DNEUPOD_HOST_ASAN=ON adds test_codecs_asan, the same tests under AddressSanitizer and UBSan (signed-overflow and shift reports are switched off: the vendored decoders wrap on corrupt data, which is harmless on ARM), and test_gapless_asan, the gapless test (the real core-1 loop, every codec pair) under the same sanitizers.

docs.title: Test vectors
docs.text:
tests/assets/audio/ holds small FLAC, MP3 and M4A files with the MD5 of their source samples, made by tools/gen_audio_vectors.py (libsndfile via uv run --no-project --with soundfile --with numpy) and tools/gen_alac_vectors.py (Apple's reference ALAC encoder built from tests/tools/alac_encoder/ with g++, plus a hand-written MP4 muxer). ctest decodes every vector and compares it bit for bit (FLAC 16-bit 44.1 kHz, 24-bit 96 kHz and 48 kHz, mono; ALAC 16-bit, 24-bit with co64, mono), checks the MP3's length and level, the demuxer's sample-table maths, the tag parsers, MD5 against the RFC 1321 vectors, the arena (including the worst-case sizes) and the core 0 / core 1 stream handshake.

Album art (tests/test_art.c, tests/test_art_snapshot.c, ctest art, art_tour, art_snapshot; pictures in tests/assets/art/, regenerated by tests/tools/gen_art_assets.py and tests/tools/make_art_flacs.py): decoded size, scale and quadrant colours of 4:2:0 600x600 / 500x333 / 1000x700, 4:4:4, 4:2:2 at an odd size, grey, restart markers and a tiny picture; progressive refused; truncated, junk and bit-flipped input; reads of 512 bytes at most and never past the picture; abort through the yield hook; cover-file ranking and the source order; APIC / PIC / PICTURE / covr positions including a 2 MB PNG and a 1.5 MB APIC that are not read; Now Playing snapshots with a cover file, an embedded JPEG, and art that cannot be shown.

docs.title: How to test (bench)
docs.text:
1. Plug the Audio Pack, headphones off your head (or very low volume). Flash neupod.elf (scripts/build.sh rp2350, then scripts/flash.sh). The splash shows the audio icon solid if the PIO and DMA stream started (the DAC cannot be detected: I2S is one-way).
  2. UART keys: w/s scroll, e select, m back, a/d left/right (volume on the Test tone screen), p play/pause.
  3. Home: s x3 to Extras, e; s to Test tone, e. Select (e) on 1 kHz tone. You should hear a quiet tone; d raises the volume 1 step = 2 dB. Try the "phones" jack (gain switch low first) and the "line out" jack. If nothing is audible see Mute line — the polarity is confirmed, so do not flip NEUPOD_AUDIO_UNMUTE_LEVEL.
  4. e again stops it. Try L/R ident (left ear first), then Scale.
  5. Files: Extras > Files, a folder with a .wav, .flac, .mp3 or .m4a, Select. Now Playing opens with the tags and format badge; the wheel (w/s) is volume; p pauses; m goes back while it keeps playing. d (Right) on a .flac runs the MD5 verify instead of playing. An .m4a with AAC says "AAC not supported yet".
  6. Album art (see UI): play tracks from folders with a cover.jpg, from 20-tags (APIC files) and from 10-matrix/19-flac-16-44-bigpng.flac (PNG: placeholder, no stall) and 20-flac-16-44-smalljpg.flac; the UART prints art: ... with the source, size, decoder scale and time. Play ALAC 24/96 while art loads: underruns must stay 0.
  7. The UART prints every 10 s the audio: line (underruns must stay 0) and the audio sink: line (actual rate, divider, dma_underruns, mute state, source, volume).

docs.title: Not verified on hardware
docs.text: Everything in this page about the board's behaviour is from reading the datasheet-level behaviour of the RP2350 PIO and DMA and from the host build; none of it has been run on the Audio Pack. The 1 kHz tone on the Audio Pack is verified (3 Nov 2026). Specifically open: the DMA interrupt timing under UI load, clock jitter, 88.2/96 kHz, SD streaming throughput at 24/32-bit, the decoders' CPU load and flash-cache behaviour on the RP2350, the 16 KB core-1 stack margin under MP3 (watch core1_stack_free in the audio: line), and the real RAM headroom (about 28 KB were left in the link).

docs.title: Bench practice and test order
docs.text: How the Pico 2 W testbed is driven from the PC, and the agreed order of the next bench tests.

docs.title: Tools and sequence
docs.text:
1. scripts/build.sh rp2350 (add --clean after a CMake option change).
  2. scripts/flash.sh [rp2350] [target] over the Debug Probe (CMSIS-DAP): programs, verifies, reset halt, then resumes core 1 and core 0. A plain OpenOCD program ... reset exit leaves core 1 halted in the bootrom (PC 0xDA) and the audio core never runs; see scripts/README.md.
  3. scripts/console.sh — UART0 at 115200 on the Debug Probe.

docs.title: Driving the UI without the wheel
docs.text:
The wheel is not fitted (the host → wheel init packet is still unknown, see Click-wheel protocol). UART keys: w/s scroll, e select, m back, a/d left/right, p play/pause, l toggles Hold (the rig has no Power key, ADR-0020). A burst of keys is queued (64 events); if the UI ever could not keep up the 10 s statistics print input: WARNING n events dropped.

  • Console lines end in \r; strip it before matching a line in a script.
  • Confirm the logged label of the highlighted row before sending Select (e); never press Select blind on a list row.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Never pkill -f <pattern> from a script: the pattern matches the script's own shell. Kill by PID.
  • Headphones off your head for the first sound from any new audio path; start with the Pack's gain switch low.
  • When a breakout is silent, read the pin state back over SWD before metering (OpenOCD mdw on SIO_IN 0xd0000004 and IO_BANK0 GPIOn_STATUS 0x40028000 + 8n, no halt needed): it separates firmware from wiring in one step.
  • Count Pico pins from pin 1 (GP0, by the USB connector); GND pins 3/8/13/18/23/28/33/38 sit next to signal pins, so an off-by-one jumper often lands on ground.
  • Record measured figures (fps, RAM, heap low-water, underruns) in the page for the feature, with the date.

docs.title: Next bench tests (agreed 3 Nov 2026)
docs.text:

  2. Display fps baseline — re-run test 7 of the display test suite (Display tests) and note the figure as the baseline for the UI-performance work.
  3. MP3 and ALAC playback (files in /Music).
  4. Settings persistence (backlight, click feedback).
  5. Haptic click per list step.
  6. SD recovery: flash mid-playback.
  7. Bluetooth scan with the AirPods in pairing mode (expect audio=yes).
  8. Battery / charging detection (VBUS + CRATE heuristic, Requirements → Power).

docs.title: Hold (Y2)
docs.text:
Steps for the Y2 after flashing a build with ADR-0020 (watch /opt/neupod-logs or the console for the ui: hold, ui: backlight and y2: power held lines):

  1. Tap Power (quick): the backlight goes off (ui: backlight off 0%) and ui: hold on follows (Auto-lock is On by default). Turn the wheel or press anything: the screen wakes, shows the pill "Locked · hold Power 2 s to unlock", and nothing else happens (no click, no Play/Pause, no selection moved).
  2. Hold Power: after about 0.4 s a blue line grows under the status bar and the pill says "Keep holding to unlock · 10 s = off"; let go at 1 s: nothing changes. Hold again to 2 s: "Unlocked", one haptic click, the lock icon leaves the status bar, ui: hold off. Keys work again.
  3. Hold Power to 2 s and on: "Locked" appears at 2 s; at 5 s the line turns red and the pill counts "Release to cancel · shutting down in 5"; let go at 7 s: nothing powers off (and nothing is lost). Repeat and hold to 10 s: ui: power-off requested, y2: power held, shutting down, the storage task stops, the player exits with status 77 and the device powers off (the wrapper's poweroff did not happen, restarting must NOT appear).
  4. With music playing and the screen locked: the headset's buttons (play/pause, next, previous) still work; the wheel and the ring buttons do not.
  5. Settings > Display: Screen off after (try 15 s) and Auto-lock Off: the screen goes off with Hold left as it was; the waking press is lost, the next one works.
  6. Charging-only mode (USB with the player "off") is unchanged: Power held 2 s reboots.

docs.title: Bluetooth: BTstack, the settings store and the plan
docs.text: Decision background: ADR-0007 (BTstack on the CYW43439 for phase 1), ADR-0011 (core 1 rules). Roles: neuPod is an A2DP source (SBC, and SBC-XQ = SBC at a high bitpool) and an AVRCP target (plus a controller side where absolute volume needs it); the headset is the sink. HFP comes later. This page covers what stage 1 and stage 2a (pairing and connection management) built, and the plan for the rest of stage 2 and for stage 3.

docs.title: Staged plan
docs.text: Stage Content State 1 RAM trim; SD-backed settings store (volume, backlight, click feedback, and BTstack's link keys); BTstack classic running on core 0; HCI bring-up; device discovery with a Settings > Bluetooth screen; host simulation built 2a Pairing (SSP "just works") and one saved headset; connection states (Pairing, Connecting, Connected, Disconnected, Failed with a reason); Connect / Disconnect / Forget; Settings > Bluetooth rows and the Devices pairing flow; link keys on the SD card; host simulation and tests. No audio. See Pairing and the connection built; bench: Pair / save / reconnect / Forget passed on a Sony WI-C200. Disconnect, re-pair after Forget, wiped-headset refusal and Wi-Fi + Bluetooth coexistence are deferred to 2b 2b A2DP source with SBC / SBC-XQ; audio routing from core 1 through a new core 1 to core 0 PCM path (storage shared with the I2S ring, ADR-0013 amendment) with the source-side pacing model below; negotiated codec on the Now Playing badge; Audio output Auto / Wired; pause on link loss; status-bar glyph. See Stage 2b. Not built: hi-res decimation, 48 kHz. built, host-tested; bench pending (Y2 first) 2c AVRCP: the headset's absolute volume is the volume (software at 0 dB), headset buttons, track metadata. See Stage 2c built, host-tested; bench pending (Y2 first) 3 Reconnect on power-up and after a drop (built, below); polish (error states, auto-sleep of the radio); the ADR-0007 listening test (SBC-XQ against a QCC3008 board, AirPods Pro 3); power measurements reconnect built, host-tested; the rest planned

docs.title: The stack
docs.text:
• BTstack from the Pico SDK 2.3.1 (lib/btstack, git eb0bb8b5e, btstack_version.h = 1.6.2): CMake targets pico_btstack_classic (HCI, L2CAP, SDP, AVDTP, A2DP, AVRCP ...), pico_btstack_hci_transport_cyw43 (HCI over the CYW43439's shared bus, with the SDK's chip support and the controller's Bluetooth firmware), pico_btstack_run_loop_async_context and pico_btstack_sbc_encoder (linked now to prove it builds; nothing calls it until stage 2, so it costs no flash). Classic only: no BLE, no mesh. Configuration: platforms/rp2350/btstack/btstack_config.h (static pools, no malloc).
  • Not used: the SDK's pico_btstack_cyw43 glue, because it stores BTstack's pairing data in the internal flash (pico_btstack_flash_bank on flash_safe_execute). See "Why the SD card" below.
  • Our glue (ADR-0019): the BTstack code is one platform-neutral adapter plus a small port per platform.
  • hal/common/bt_btstack/bt_btstack.c implements the Bluetooth half of hal/include/hal_radio.h (hal_bt_*): discovery, the pairing and connection state machine, the timeouts, and the link key database on top of the settings store (hal_bt_storage_t, wrapped as a btstack_tlv_t). Nothing BTstack-specific crosses hal_radio.h. hal/host/hal_radio.c is the host simulator.
  • hal/common/bt_btstack/bt_port.h is what a platform provides: bt_port_present() (is the controller usable), bt_port_start() (memory, run loop and hci_init() with the platform's transport), bt_port_run_sync() and bt_port_post() (hand work to BTstack's thread, blocking or not), bt_port_power(), bt_port_storage() (the storage BTstack's thread may use), bt_port_deliver() and bt_port_poll() (events out). The local address comes from the controller on the RP2350; the Y2 port reads it before HCI starts. No locking is part of the port: the adapter's state is touched by BTstack's thread only, or through atomics.
  • RP2350: platforms/rp2350/hal/bt_port_cyw43.c: the CYW43 transport, the async_context run loop, and the SDK's btstack_cyw43_init() / btstack_cyw43_deinit() hooks (cyw43_arch_init() calls them), as before the split.
  • Y2: platforms/y2/hal/bt_port_stpbt.c: /dev/stpbt through btstack_uart_stpbt.c (one H4 packet per read(), the device is not a tty) and btstack_chipset_mtk_consys.c (the MediaTek vendor script that must run before HCI_Reset), both shared with the y2-a2dp bench tool (testbed/y2/tools/y2-a2dp), and the POSIX run loop on a thread of its own. Configuration: platforms/y2/btstack/btstack_config.h; BTstack's source list is cmake/btstack_posix.cmake (the Pico SDK's copy, as for the tool).
  • Controller: the CYW43439 on the Pico 2 W. Its Bluetooth device address is the Wi-Fi MAC plus one (the SDK transport sets it). CYW43_ENABLE_BLUETOOTH=1 is set once for everything that links neupod_freertos, because cyw43_arch_init() is compiled into several static libraries and every copy must agree.

docs.title: Threading
docs.text:
BTstack is single-threaded; which thread that is depends on the port. Every hal_bt_* call can be made from any RTOS task and only hands a request over (bt_port_post()) or reads an atomic; the BTstack code itself runs on one thread.

RP2350. BTstack runs on the async context of the CYW43 driver, which with pico_cyw43_arch_sys_freertos is one FreeRTOS task, the "CYW43 worker" (core 0, priority 3, 6 KB stack; it was 4 KB before BTstack). Every BTstack callback, and our packet handler, runs on that task.

Caller How it reaches BTstack Blocks the caller? radio boot check (hal_bt_init) async_context_execute_sync (bt_port_run_sync) yes, until the worker has queued the HCI power-on (milliseconds) UI task (hal_bt_inquiry_start / _stop; stage 2a: hal_bt_pair / _connect / _disconnect / _forget) btstack_run_loop_execute_on_main_thread (bt_port_post; a static callback registration each; the state is reserved with an atomic exchange first, so one request is in flight) no radio worker to the UI hal_bt_event_fn callback (bt_port_deliver calls it at once), which app/runtime/bt_service.c turns into a 16-deep queue (os_queue_send, no wait: an event is dropped rather than holding the radio up) no

Core 1 never calls any of this, and BTstack never runs on it. The rules in Runtime hold unchanged; tools/check_core1_closure.py is still green on the linked image.

Y2. The firmware is a Linux process whose RTOS is the FreeRTOS POSIX port: tasks are pthreads that the port runs one at a time and its critical sections are global state, so a thread that is not an RTOS task must never call a FreeRTOS function (queue, mutex, event group, delay). BTstack therefore runs on the POSIX run loop on a pthread of its own (512 KB stack, every signal blocked, including the port's SIGALRM tick, which is sent to the running task's thread only). It never calls the app and never touches the settings store:

Direction How task to BTstack bt_port_post(): tasks take turns (an atomic flag, sleeping through the scheduler) and call btstack_run_loop_execute_on_main_thread, whose own native lock then only BTstack's thread and one task contend for. hal_bt_init waits with hal_delay_ms (scheduler sleep), up to 15 s, never a native wait BTstack to the app events go into a 64-slot lock-free ring; hal_bt_poll() (the UI frame calls it through bt_service_tick) delivers them from the calling task, in order, one task at a time. The callback therefore runs on that task, not on the radio thread: same rules (quick, no blocking, no calls back into hal_bt_*). A ring that overflows drops the new event and says so on the console link keys platforms/y2/hal/y2_bt_tlv.c: BTstack's thread reads and writes a RAM copy of the link-key records (preloaded from the settings store in hal_bt_init); the same poll writes changes back to the store, retrying about once a second while the store refuses (no card, read-only, not loaded). Pairing works without a writable card; the key then lives for the session only

Start-up on the Y2: hal_system_late_init() calls y2_bt_probe(), which reads /data/BT_Addr (read only, 6 bytes, MSB first; an unreadable, short, all-zero or all-0xFF file means Bluetooth unavailable, never a default address) and opens /dev/stpbt on a helper thread with signals blocked (the open powers the chip and takes about 1.3 s). Bluetooth is available only if both worked. The descriptor is kept and handed to the transport, so the device is opened once. hal_bt_init then sets BTstack up (the MediaTek vendor script, with the address, runs before HCI_Reset), starts the thread and powers HCI on. There is no Wi-Fi on the Y2 (hal_wifi_present() is false), so the boot check reports Wi-Fi unavailable while Bluetooth is available. Chip bring-up before the firmware starts is S80mtk-bt (Y2 testbed).

The controller does not report a page timeout at the configured time (the MT6582 only answers after Create_Connection_Cancel), so an unanswered Pair or Connect is ended by our own timer (HAL_BT_PAIR_TIMEOUT_MS / HAL_BT_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS), which cancels the page and ends the attempt as "timed out"; a late Connection_Complete with an error is ignored.

docs.title: Boot and what the UART shows
docs.text:
The "radio" boot check task (4.8 s deadline, then it keeps waiting up to 12 s so a slow bring-up still upgrades the result) calls hal_system_late_init() (CYW43 driver, which also starts BTstack's memory and run loop through btstack_cyw43_init), then bt_service_start(), which sets the local name (neuPod), the Class of Device (Audio, portable audio), makes the device never discoverable, and not connectable or bondable (nobody can find it; only while a Pair action runs is it connectable and bondable, for the chosen headset only, stage 2a) and calls hci_power_control(HCI_POWER_ON).

Expected UART lines (about 1 to 3 s after the splash starts; the exact time is a thing to measure on the board):

bt: HCI up, local BD_ADDR 28:CD:C1:xx:xx:xx
bt: BTstack 1.6.2; controller HCI version 11 (Bluetooth 5.2) revision 0x.... , LMP 11, manufacturer 0x.... , LMP subversion 0x....
boot: bluetooth ok      : HCI up, BD_ADDR 28:CD:C1:xx:xx:xx
boot: wifi      DEGRADED: no Wi-Fi driver yet (Bluetooth comes first)
boot: chk_radio  task stack free min .... B
settings: no file yet (defaults) (0 items, seq 0)      (or: loaded (n items, seq n))

(The version numbers are what the controller reports; the values above are only the expected shape.) If HCI does not come up: bt: HCI did not come up or bt: hci_power_control(ON) failed (n) and the check shows "bluetooth stack down".

docs.title: Discovery
docs.text:
hal_bt_inquiry_start(10) runs a general inquiry for 10 s (8 units of 1.28 s). Each result carries the address, the Class of Device, the signal strength (RSSI) and the name when it was in the extended inquiry response. The inquiry mode is set to "RSSI and extended inquiry response" (hci_set_inquiry_mode(INQUIRY_MODE_RSSI_AND_EIR) before power-on); BTstack's default is the plain mode, which carries neither. If the controller refuses the Inquiry command (BTstack gives no event for that) the scan ends at once with bt: inquiry refused by the controller (status 0x..). Audio sinks are devices whose Class of Device major class is Audio/Video (bits 12..8 = 4: headsets, speakers, car kits). After the inquiry the radio asks for the names of audio devices that had none, one at a time (at most 6; a name request cannot overlap an inquiry). Up to 12 devices are kept per scan. Stopping a scan skips the name requests.

Settings > Bluetooth (UI) is a short page (Audio output, Devices, Absolute volume). Devices starts the scan as it opens (unless audio is streaming) and lists the remembered headset first, then everything found as it arrives: audio devices (strongest first once the scan ends), then others greyed out with "(phone)" and the like, each with a three-bar signal; the last row is Stop scanning / Scan again and four dots at the bottom show a scan running. Selecting an audio device pairs with it (stage 2a, below). Menu goes back and stops the scan.

bt_service_pair / _connect / _disconnect / _forget (app/runtime/bt_service.c) are what the UI calls. Link events are handled in the radio callback, not by a screen, so a Pair that finishes while the user has left the screen is still remembered.

UI (UI, design review BT-1 to BT-3): on Devices the remembered headset is the first row, its state on the right (Connected / Streaming / Saved / Pairing... / Connecting... / Reconnecting... / No audio / Failed: reason, with busy dots while working); Select on it opens Connect (or Disconnect, Cancel) and Forget (a question screen: Select = Forget, Menu = Keep). Select on a found audio device stops the scan if needed and starts the Pair action; the row says "Pairing..." with busy dots, then the device becomes the remembered headset at the top, or the row says Failed: reason. Menu cancels a Pair in progress (so the radio does not stay connectable for nobody). With a headset already remembered the choice is "Replace with ?" (Select = yes): the old one is disconnected, the new one paired once the radio is free, and the old key is deleted when the new one is saved. The audio output setting is Auto / Wired / Bluetooth (BT-3; stored as 0 / 1 / 2, a stored value this firmware does not know reads as Auto): Bluetooth makes the output Bluetooth at once and keeps it through a Disconnect; Play with no headset pauses with "Headset not connected" and nothing comes out of the wired output. Absolute volume is shown read-only. Not built: Bluetooth On / Off (the radio drivers have no clean power-down), renaming a headset.

The link as toasts. The frame (ui_frame.c) turns the link's life into toasts: " disconnected . reconnecting..." when a connected headset is lost (bt_service_lost_seq(): only for a loss, not for the power-up attempt), " connected" (info, 1.2 s) when the automatic reconnect succeeds (bt_service_reconnected_seq()), "Couldn't reconnect - paused" when it gives up (bt_service_gave_up_seq()). ADR-0019 stands: playback pauses and stays on Bluetooth; the firmware never switches the output by itself.

Failure stance. Fail closed for the radio: connectable and bondable go off on every way out of a Pair (success, failure, timeout, cancel, leaving the screen, the stack going down), and the 30 s timer is the backstop. Never discoverable. A saved device is written only on success. Fail open for the features: with no card the saved headset and the keys live in RAM for the session (as the store always does).

Known limit of 2a. Nothing holds the link open (the A2DP signalling channel arrives in 2b), so the link closes by itself shortly after the SDP query: by BTstack's idle timeout, or by the headset itself (reason 0x13, remote user terminated, seen on the bench after 1 to 2 s with a Sony WI-C200; BTstack's own idle timeout would be later). Both are reported as DISCONNECTED and logged as bt: link closed <addr> reason 0x.. (idle), not as failures; only abnormal endings (supervision timeout and the like) are LINK_LOST. No keep-alive is added. The 2a UI worded a CONNECTED link "Paired, no audio yet"; stage 2b opens the A2DP stream right after CONNECTED, which keeps the link up, and the row says "Connected - SBC" / "Streaming" (Stage 2b).

Pairing method. Only Secure Simple Pairing (2.1 and later) is supported. With "no input, no output" IO capability the key is unauthenticated (LEVEL_2, "just works"), which is all a headset needs. A pre-2.1 headset that asks for a PIN is refused at once (gap_pin_code_negative) and the Pair ends FAILED "PIN not supported". SSP headsets only.

Teardown. If the link drops during bonding, SDP or authentication from the other side (or by timeout), or locally during SDP or authentication, the attempt ends at once as FAILED (a local disconnect is ignored only while bonding: BTstack sends one itself after a failed bonding and the real bonding result follows), so the Pair window closes without waiting for the timer. Cancelling a connection that is still being created retries hci_create_connection_cancel every 200 ms (at most 10 times) when the controller cannot take a command yet. Every Pair / Connect has an attempt number: a disconnect request or an SDP result that belongs to an earlier attempt cannot end the next one (a query still running from a cancelled attempt makes the next one wait for the SDP client). When BTstack reports the stack OFF, a link or attempt in progress becomes FAILED (INTERNAL) and everything is reset.

Pairing order. Pair uses gap_dedicated_bonding and keeps the link for the SDP query: btstack_config.h defines ENABLE_EXPLICIT_DEDICATED_BONDING_DISCONNECT, so BTstack reports a good bonding at once and does not disconnect (a failed bonding still disconnects). Without that define the result is only reported after a disconnect, and every Pair timed out (found on the bench). gap_dedicated_bonding deletes any old key for the address first, which is what a re-pair wants; Connect cannot use it for that very reason. On real hardware the bonding result arrives before the link-key notification: neither the stray-key filter nor the candidate logic depends on the order (the Pair is still in progress when the key arrives, and a headset is only remembered after the SDP check).

Console lines (bt_btstack.c, bt_saved.c): bt: pair <addr>, bt: connect <addr>, bt: connected <addr>, bt: <addr> failed: <text>, bt: link lost 0x.. (abnormal end of an established link), bt: link closed <addr> reason 0x.. (idle, no profile yet) (clean idle drop), bt: link dropped in set-up 0x.., bt: bonding 0x.., bt: dropped stray key <addr>, bt: forgot <addr>, bt: pair not persisted (store not writable), bt: key delete waits (store not writable), bt: record kept (store not writable).

docs.title: Stage 2b to-do from the 2a review
docs.text:
• Bench: Disconnect, re-pair after Forget, a headset that wiped its key (Connect must refuse), Wi-Fi + Bluetooth coexistence.
  • A host test that links hal/common/bt_btstack/bt_btstack.c against a BTstack stub and injects event sequences (bonding failure 0x16 then 0xD9, remote 0x13 during SDP, timeout in each phase, stack off mid-attempt, Forget of the current peer, PIN request). Today only the simulator in hal/host/hal_radio.c is tested.
  • A boot-time sweep that drops any BTstack link key whose address is not the saved record (orphan keys after a damaged record or a power cut before the stale queue drains).

docs.title: Wi-Fi alongside Bluetooth (provisional)
docs.text: Stuart's decision for stage 2: allow both; Wi-Fi follows its own "Wi-Fi while playing" setting and no interlock is built. This is provisional: the CYW43439 shares one radio and one bus between Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, and the decision may be revisited after bench testing. The policy lives in one place, NEUPOD_BT_WIFI_COEX_ALLOW in app/include/runtime_config.h (default 1); a future interlock hangs off it at bt_service_pair() / bt_service_connect() and in wifi_service. With 1 nothing is checked anywhere. Bench check (stage 2a): Wi-Fi joined and an NTP / HTTP transfer running, then Pair, Connect and Disconnect: no HCI reset, no dropped link, no Wi-Fi drop, and the 6 KB radio-worker stack minimum (chk_radio / the worker line) stays above its stage 1 value. Stage 2b repeats it with an A2DP stream.

docs.title: Why the SD card holds the pairing data (and never the internal flash)
docs.text:
BTstack normally keeps link keys and its device database in a TLV store in the last sectors of the internal QSPI flash. Erasing or programming that flash at run time means the XIP flash cannot be read for the duration (milliseconds to tens of milliseconds). Core 1 executes its code from that same flash (only the hot path is in RAM) and is deliberately not multicore_lockout-aware (ADR-0011: no RTOS, no locks, no cross-core stop requests), so a flash write from core 0 would stall or crash the audio core. Therefore nothing in this firmware writes the internal flash at run time, and the image contains none of pico_flash, flash_safe_execute or btstack_tlv_flash_bank code paths in use (checked on the linked ELF).

Link keys and the device database are stored in the settings store instead, a small file on the microSD card:

API app/include/settings_store.h, app/settings/settings_store.c; RTOS glue app/runtime/settings_service.c Content tag (32-bit) to value (up to 96 bytes), up to 48 tags (SETTINGS_MAX_ITEMS; worst case about 41 with the saved headset): volume (NPvo), backlight (NPbl), auto-dim and its idle time (NPad/NPat), output path of the saved volume (NPvp), the resume record (NPr0/NPr1, Audio), shuffle and repeat (NPsh/NPrp), click mode (NPck: 0 off, 1 haptic, 2 piezo, 3 both), haptic actuator (NPha) and calibration (NPhc), Wi-Fi settings and networks (Wi-Fi), BTstack link keys (BTL + slot 0..7, 28 bytes plaintext, stored sealed since the secrets work, up to 8), the remembered headset (NPbd, 10 to 42 bytes, stage 2a) and later device records. The same tag/value/length model as BTstack's TLV, so hal_bt_storage_t (in hal_radio.h) maps one to one onto btstack_tlv_t File two alternating files /.neupod/settings.a and settings.b: magic NPST, version (2; version-1 files, same layout and at most 32 items, are still read), count, sequence number, items, CRC-32. Little endian. About 4.9 KB at most (48 tags x 101 bytes). Firmware older than the version-2 store does not read these files: it sets them aside as "newer" and starts from defaults (it never overwrites them), so a rollback loses the settings but not the file Reading settings_load() on the storage task right after the card mounted. A file that fails magic, version or CRC gives defaults (reported on the UART, replaced by the next save). A newer or older layout is treated the same way Crash-safe save no rename and no delete. The image is written in place over the OLDER (or invalid) of the two files and synced; the other file is never touched. Load takes the valid file with the higher sequence (wrap-safe), so a power cut at any point leaves at least the previous complete state; a torn file just fails its CRC. A file with a NEWER layout version is moved aside as settings.old at the next save instead of being wiped (firmware rollback). Host tests cut the power during the write, again during a rewrite after a cut, and on the very first save Who writes only the storage task (settings_service_poll: it wakes every 500 ms when idle and looks at the store at most every 250 ms). The first unsaved change is written about 1.5 s later, so a burst of wheel clicks is one write; a failed save is retried after 5 s. No save while audio is playing (an SD card can stall for far longer than the audio ring lasts): changes wait for pause, stop, the end of the track or an idle moment, then are written. The cost is that a volume change made during a long track is lost if the power fails before the next pause. While paused the ring is full and nothing consumes it, so a write cannot hurt. Core 1 never touches it No card / degraded the store is RAM-only: every setter and the BTstack storage still work for the session, nothing is written, the UART says so. After 3 failed saves in a row the store stops trying (RAM-only) until restart. Failure stance: fail safe for the card (no write is attempted when the card or its mount is not healthy) and fail open for the features (settings and pairing keep working in RAM) Reads before the load BTstack writes are refused until the store knows whether there is a card and has loaded it (the load would otherwise throw them away). With no card at all they are accepted for the session

docs.title: How the write lock is opened, and only for this file
docs.text:
The card is write-locked by default (hal_storage_set_write_enabled(false)). settings_flush() is the only production code that opens it, and it does so in one fixed pattern:

  1. nfs_write_scope_enter("/.neupod"): from now until nfs_write_scope_leave() every mutating nfs_* call (open for write, mkdir, unlink, rename, with both paths) whose normalised path is not /.neupod itself or below it fails with NFS_ERR_IO, on the card and on the host. .. is resolved before the check and the comparison is by path component (/.neupod2 is outside).
  2. hal_storage_set_write_enabled(true) (remembering the previous state).
  3. save (the five steps above).
  4. hal_storage_set_write_enabled(previous), then the scope is left. There is one exit path, so a failed or "power lost" save restores both.

What this does not cover, stated plainly: FatFs updates the FAT and the directory entries that belong to files inside /.neupod, and those sectors are shared with the rest of the volume; the scope limits which files can be changed, not which sectors the file system touches while changing them. It also does not stop a raw hal_storage_write(), which nothing else in the firmware calls outside the storage test menus. The store never formats, never creates or deletes anything outside /.neupod, and its paths are compile-time constants. The scope is not recursive and is meant for one caller on one task, so it has no lock.

docs.title: Volume restore policy
docs.text:
The saved volume is restored at boot after the load, but never louder than the power-on default (-30 dB, player_restore_volume, headphone safety, see Audio), and only if the user has not changed the volume yet in this session. A saved quiet level (for example -40 dB) comes back; a saved loud level (for example -10 dB) comes back as -30 dB. The constant is PLAYER_RESTORE_MIN_ATT_DB.

Replacement (design response, 3 Nov 2026; built in player_volume_restore_att()): honour the saved level, except cap at -30 dB when

  • the output path differs from the one the level was saved for (Bluetooth ↔ wired ↔ line/optical), or
  • a headphone insertion is detected at boot and the saved path was line-out.

The output path is stored alongside the level in the settings store (NPvp, an output_path_t: wired, line, optical, Bluetooth). Conservative readings taken where the text is silent: a level saved without a path (older firmware) or a restore when the current path is unknown is capped; line-out and optical count as different paths (any change of path is a change); a level already quieter than -30 dB is never touched. Nothing in the firmware reports the output path yet (no Bluetooth audio routing, no jack detect), so until a source calls player_set_output_path() / player_set_headphones_at_boot() every restore is capped at -30 dB, exactly as before; the policy, the stored path and the tests are in place.

docs.title: Memory budget (RP2350, main SRAM 512 KB)
docs.text:
Since 12 Nov 2026 this is history, not a limit: the Pico 2 W build is frozen (compile-only regression check) and its 520 KB is no longer a budget; the product target is the RP2350B with PSRAM (ADR-0001 amendment). The figures stay as the record of what the testbed ran.

The static RAM ("bss", every figure from arm-none-eabi-size on the linked neupod.elf):

before (feat/codecs) after stage 1 FreeRTOS heap (NEUPOD_RTOS_HEAP_BYTES) 112 KB 80 KB LVGL pool (NEUPOD_LVGL_POOL_BYTES) 96 KB 72 KB (the host tour still passes) codec arena 116 KB 116 KB settings store (items, parse buffers) 0 about 5.3 KB at the end of stage 1; 12.7 KB with Wi-Fi (Wi-Fi) and 32 items; about 9.9 KB now with 48 items (items 5.0 KB + one 4.9 KB image buffer: the load validates the two files in the buffer and parses the winner straight into the items, so there are no staging copies) BTstack (HCI buffers, pools) and the Bluetooth HAL 0 about 6.6 KB bss total 481,588 B 436,480 B (45,108 B freed) flash image (text) 1,060,732 B 1,120,532 B (+59,800 B: BTstack classic, transport, settings, UI)

The two constants are in app/os/memory_budget.h. Heap consumers that grew: the CYW43 worker stack (4 to 6 KB), a transient 4 KB boot-check stack for the radio check, the Bluetooth event queue (about 1 KB) and the settings mutex. The monitor prints the heap low-water mark and the LVGL pool peak every 10 s, which is the number to check on the board (earlier bench figures: heap minimum free about 58 KB of 112 KB, LVGL peak about 38 KB, both before this change).

Stage 2a delta (clean Release builds of main at 4944981 and of the branch, arm-none-eabi-size on neupod.elf):

main stage 2a delta flash image (text) 1,263,280 B 1,285,888 B +22,608 B (SDP client and L2CAP now linked and used, the pairing state machine, the saved-headset module, the UI rows) data 0 0 0 static RAM (bss) 488,896 B 489,340 B +444 B (L2CAP and SDP client state, the link state machine, the saved-device candidate and the four-deep key-deletion queue) free SRAM (__HeapLimit - __end__) 15,320 B 14,876 B -444 B

BTstack heap use: none. HAVE_MALLOC is not defined and every pool is a static array in .bss; the pool counts in btstack_config.h did not change (the 444 B above is everything that moved). The FreeRTOS heap and the task stacks are unchanged; the new code runs on the 6 KB radio-worker stack, so its high-water mark is on the bench list. No internal-flash write code is linked (flash_safe_execute, pico_flash, btstack_tlv_flash_bank are absent from the ELF). The core-1 closure check reports ok.

BTstack pools (btstack_config.h) are sized for one headset: 1 HCI connection, 4 L2CAP channels, 1 AVDTP connection, 2 stream endpoints, 2 AVRCP entries (the two roles of one link, since 2c), 8 remembered link keys (the UI remembers one headset; the other seven slots are headroom); ACL buffers 1021 + 4 bytes. Stage 2a needs 1 HCI connection and 1 L2CAP channel (the SDP query), so they were not touched. Revisit them in 2b when the real stream is up.

docs.title: Licence
docs.text: BTstack is not free for commercial use. Its own licence is non-commercial only; Raspberry Pi holds a grant that lets purchasers of its Pico W / Pico 2 W / RM2 products use it in their products. The details, and what is not settled, are in the third-party table of LICENSE.md. In short: fine on the Pico 2 W bench rig; a final board with a bare CYW43439 chip (or any non-Raspberry-Pi radio route) needs a written answer from BlueKitchen / Raspberry Pi, or a commercial BTstack licence, before anything is sold or distributed. The cyw43-driver has the same shape of licence (non-commercial, with a Raspberry Pi grant for use with its chips).

docs.title: Stage 2b: the audio stream (built)
docs.text:
Headroom. The Bluetooth output is attenuated by a fixed NEUPOD_BT_HEADROOM_DB (3 dB, audio_dsp.h) before the 16-bit conversion (TPDF-dithered) and SBC. Found on the Y2 with AirPods Pro (12 Nov 2026): with a track mastered to 0 dBFS at volume 0 dB, the decoded SBC put 80 to 135 samples per 2 s at the rail in loud passages, heard as crackle; the PCM into the encoder was bit-exact and the SBC stream matched a reference encode on the PC (22 to 27 dB SNR), so the overshoot is SBC's own reconstruction. At -4 dB it was clean. The headset's volume (AVRCP, stage 2c) makes up the level. Bench aids on the Y2 only: NEUPOD_BT_HCI_DUMP=<file> (HCI trace, PacketLogger format) and NEUPOD_BT_PCM_DUMP=<file> (the encoder's input PCM) in /etc/neupod-fw.env.

Built and host-tested; not yet run on a headset in the firmware (bench steps at the end). The Y2 is where it is proved first: the BTstack A2DP source it uses is the one verified on AirPods Pro and a Sony WI-C200 by the y2-a2dp tool, now inside the shared adapter.

The stream. Once the link is CONNECTED the adapter opens an A2DP source stream by itself (a2dp_source_establish_stream) with one SBC endpoint: 44.1 kHz stereo, joint stereo, 16 blocks, 8 subbands, bitpool up to the headset's maximum but at most 53 (328 kbit/s). NEUPOD_BT_SBC_XQ=1 raises the cap to 76 (455 kbit/s); the badge then reads SBC-XQ whenever the bitpool in use is above 53. Both are constants at the top of hal/common/bt_btstack/bt_btstack.c. The stream is reported as HAL_BT_EVT_STREAM (OPENING, OPEN, STREAMING, SUSPENDED, CLOSED, FAILED with a reason) with the negotiated hal_bt_codec_t; hal_bt_stream_start / suspend / close / open are asynchronous requests to BTstack's thread, and hal_bt_stats() gives frames encoded, packets sent, underruns, drift corrections and the link RSSI where the controller reports it. A headset that offers no usable configuration fails with "no common format"; one that refuses the stream with "audio refused".

Where the PCM comes from. PCM never passes through hal_bt_*. The audio core (core 1) has a second output: with audio_set_output(AUDIO_OUT_BT, 44100) its sink is virtual (hal_audio_set_virtual: the block clock still ticks every 256 frames at the sample rate, nothing leaves a DAC) and the block interrupt writes each block, rounded to 16 bit (with TPDF dither when the volume is below 0 dB or the source is deeper than 16 bit) into a Bluetooth ring, app/audio/bt_pcm.c. The encoder (BTstack's thread) is the one consumer, through hal_bt_set_pcm_source() (hal/include/hal_bt_pcm.h), lock-free, no RTOS call (on the Y2 BTstack's thread is not an RTOS task). Core 1 keeps the ADR-0011 rules; tools/check_core1_closure.py is green with the new roots (vclk_isr) and bt_pcm.c is in the source-rule list.

One store for both rings (ADR-0013 amendment). The 32 KB g_pcm_store has two layouts that never coexist: wired = the whole store is the decoder ring (4096 frames of int32 stereo); Bluetooth = its first half is the decoder ring (2048 frames, 46 ms at 44.1 kHz) and its second half is the Bluetooth ring (4096 frames of int16 stereo, 93 ms). The layout changes only with the stream closed (AUDIO_CMD_OUTPUT). No new static RAM for the rings.

Pacing, link first. The headset's clock is not ours, so nothing is a free-running clock:

  • The Bluetooth ring is the only buffer between the decoder and the link. When it has no room for a block the block interrupt waits (consumes nothing, advances no position, counts bt_stall_blocks): the decoder, the elapsed time and the end of the track are paced by the link.
  • The encoder is a run-loop timer (8 ms) that owes the headset rate x elapsed time of audio, never more than the catch-up budget of it (160 ms; it was a hard 40 ms cap until the Y2 walk, see Link robustness), and while a finished packet waits for "can send now" it produces nothing. The owed amount is steered by the ring's fill level against half of it: above half the encoder consumes up to 0.3 % faster, below half slower, one step of 0.05 % per tick; each change of step is a "drift correction" in the statistics. When a stream starts the excess above half (the ring filled during the set-up) is sent at once, within a 40 ms bound (BT_LINK_STALL_MS).
  • An empty ring while a track plays is an underrun (counted once per dry spell, not per tick); an empty ring while paused is not (active() of the source). What was owed during an underrun is dropped: no burst when audio returns.
  • The SBC storage bound includes the payload header byte (the y2-a2dp review fix): the packet holds at most min(link MTU - 1, storage - 1) bytes of frames. 680 B of storage on the RP2350 (a typical headset MTU is 672), 1030 B on the Y2.

Routing (app/runtime/audio_route.c). The saved setting Audio output: Auto / Wired (Settings > Bluetooth; default Auto). Auto: Bluetooth as soon as a headset's stream is open. Once the output is Bluetooth it stays Bluetooth until the headset is let go on purpose (Disconnect or Forget) or the setting is Wired. The change needs a quiet audio core: whatever plays is stopped (its place is kept, as for Stop), the audio stream is closed, the output selected, the stream reopened. The A2DP stream is started when something plays and suspended after 4 s of silence. Link lost while playing: the player is paused at once (position kept), the ring is emptied (honoured by the consumer at its next call), the banner "Headset disconnected" shows for 3 s, nothing plays from the wired output. Play pressed with no headset on the Bluetooth output pauses again with "Headset not connected". A stream the headset released while the link stays up is reopened up to three times.

What is not in 2b (deviations from ADR-0019 and the brief).

  • Sample rate: 44.1 kHz only. The endpoint offers 44.1 kHz; a track at another rate (48 kHz, 88.2 / 96 kHz) is refused on the Bluetooth output ("Not supported on Bluetooth (44.1 kHz only)", and the queue skips it) because there is no resampler and ADR-0003 forbids a cheap one. 48 kHz would need a stream reconfiguration per track (or a resampler); the hi-res decimation on core 1 (half-band FIR, 2:1 / 4:1) of ADR-0013 is a follow-up, not built: its coefficients and state have to be measured against the closure check and the 7.7 KB of free SRAM.
  • Volume is the software volume as on I2S in 2b (absolute volume, the headset keys and the track information are 2c).
  • hal_bt_set_pcm_source is an addition to the HAL: ADR-0019 says PCM does not go through hal_bt_*; this call only hands the stack the consumer side of the ring.
  • The status-bar glyph for "connected" is the text colour, not white: the bar is light.

Memory (RP2350, Release, arm-none-eabi-size on neupod.elf, the phase 1 branch before and after):

before 2b after 2b delta flash image (text) 1,297,748 B 1,349,812 B +52,064 B (A2DP / AVDTP / the SBC encoder, routing, UI) static RAM (bss) 489,712 B 496,536 B +6,824 B (SBC encoder state 1,704, SBC packet storage 680, PCM scratch 512 + 1,024, AVDTP / A2DP / SDP pools and records, 16-bit block buffer, the longer 48-byte names) free SRAM (__HeapLimit - __end__) about 14.5 KB 7,680 B -6.8 KB

The rings add nothing (shared store).
