  • This view is the one place the UI uses the panel's colour depth heavily; on the AMOLED candidate the black background also saves power.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
• Two-pane: list of settings groups on the left, a live detail pane on the right for the highlighted group (shown: Bluetooth — connected device, codec, battery).
  • Select enters a group; inside, scroll changes the value and Select confirms.
  • "Click" is where the piezo / haptic / both / off choice lives (the piezo has no driver yet), and "Haptics" holds the actuator (ERM / LRA) and Calibrate rows; hardware decision in Requirements → Reused parts and mechanical.
  • "Output" chooses headphone / line / optical / USB when the jack detect cannot decide.

docs.title: Resolution profiles
docs.text:
The product panel is 320x240 and the mock-ups above are drawn at that size, but the firmware UI is resolution-independent (ADR-0018): every pixel size lives in one struct, ui_metrics_t (app/ui/ui_metrics.h, values in app/ui/ui_metrics.c), and ui_task picks the profile once, after hal_display_init(), from hal_display_width() / hal_display_height() (the largest profile that fits the panel; 320x240 when none does). Screens read UIM->... (the active profile); UI_W, UI_H, UI_STATUS_H, UI_CONTENT_H, UI_ROW_H and UI_ROWS_VISIBLE in ui_internal.h are shorthands for its first fields. Nothing outside ui_metrics.c scales a length.

320x240 (product panel) 480x360 (Y2 testbed, host NEUPOD_DISPLAY_SIZE=480x360) Status bar / list row 24 / 30 px 36 / 45 px Content area, rows per page 216 px, 7 324 px, 7 Fonts small / body / large / huge Montserrat 12 / 14 / 20 / 48 (own build, Latin-1) Montserrat 16 / 20 / 28 / 48 Icons (Lucide, 1-bit) small / large 16 / 24 px 24 / 36 px Home split (list / pane), art box 179 / 141 (56 %), 117 px 269 / 211, 175 px Now Playing art box, text column 112 px at (14, 14), x = 140 168 px at (21, 21), x = 210 Settings split (groups / summary) 179 / 141 269 / 211 Splash icon, icon row, wordmark 32 px, y = 116, 48 pt 48 px, y = 174, 48 pt (the largest size built) LVGL partial-render buffers 2 x 320 x 24 RGB565 (15 KB each) 2 x 480 x 36 (34 KB each; hosted builds only) Toast / HUD strip, lock pill 22 / 26 / 24 px 33 / 39 / 36 px

The 480x360 profile is every length of the 320x240 one times 3/2 (the S() macro in ui_metrics.c, used only in that table), and fonts step to the next size (14 to 20, 20 to 28: 1.43x and 1.4x, a little under 1.5x, so text that fits at 320 fits at 480). Row counts do not change: both profiles show 7 rows. Adding a profile is one more initialiser in ui_metrics.c; tests/test_ui_metrics.c checks every compiled-in profile (title bar and rows fit the height, art box fits above the progress bar, text lines stack without overlapping, the splash debug list fits between the icon row and the version, the static LVGL buffers are big enough) and pins the 320x240 numbers to what the UI had before profiles existed.

What is compiled where. NEUPOD_UI_HIRES (CMake option; default ON for NEUPOD_PLATFORM=host and y2, OFF for rp2350 and esp32s3) adds the 480x360 profile, Montserrat 28 (lv_conf.h), 480-wide render buffers (UI_BUF_W_MAX), a 192 KB LVGL pool (memory_budget.h) and the layout audit (ui_audit.c). Without it the product build has the one 320x240 profile as a compile-time constant, so the RP2350 image is unchanged (flash and RAM identical in size; see the ADR). A hosted build still picks its profile at run time, so a host built with the option runs the 320x240 layout byte for byte as before unless told otherwise.

Host. NEUPOD_DISPLAY_SIZE=WxH (read once; between 320x240 and 640x480, default 320x240) sets the simulated panel size. NEUPOD_UI_AUDIT=1 makes every snapshot also walk the widget tree and print ui: AUDIT FAIL ... for a visible widget that lies outside the panel or its container (one pixel over the container's far edge is tolerated; only the list's off-window pool rows may be clipped away) and for a label whose text does not fit its box (dots / scrolling labels are not measured). Each snapshot prints ui: audit '<name>' WxH objects=N violations=V; the tests require that line. At start-up the UI logs ui: profile WxH on WxH panel and warns when the panel is bigger than the profile (including a build without NEUPOD_UI_HIRES on a panel above 320x240). ctest runs the tours at 480x360 as hires_tour, hires_input_tour, hires_wifi_tour, hires_bt_tour and hires_art_tour (snapshots in build/host/snapshots_hires*, checked by hires_art_snapshot), and the default runtime_smoke tour runs the audit at 320x240. Each hires test has its own fake card, so ctest -j3 (as CI runs it) is safe; the 320x240 tours share one card and hold a resource lock. neupod exits 3 when fewer snapshots were written than the tour promised (typically --run-ms too short), 2 when the audio task starved, 4 without audio stats.

Known limits at 480x360. The album art is still decoded to a 64 x 64 thumbnail (ART_MAX_DIM, art.h; 8 KB of static RAM on the product build) and scaled up by LVGL, 2.6x into the 168 px box, so it is softer than at 320x240. The 48 pt splash wordmark and the note glyph do not grow (48 is the largest size built). The bring-up scenes (gfx_strip, now_playing_draw, the display test menu) are 320x240 only.

docs.title: Fonts and display text
docs.text:
The UI draws with its own builds of Montserrat Medium (SIL OFL 1.1) at 12 (Small), 14, 16 (Small at 480x360, hosted builds only), 20, 28 (480x360, hosted builds only) and 48 pt, 4 bpp, merged with the few Font Awesome symbols that are still drawn from the fonts (LV_SYMBOL_*: note, tick, image, Wi-Fi, battery 3, Bluetooth, SD card, none of which the boot splash uses any more; the rest of the symbols moved to the Lucide icons, below). They are generated files in app/ui/fonts/ (tools/gen_ui_fonts.sh rebuilds them; the command line, sources and licences are in app/ui/fonts/README.md) and replace LVGL's built-in lv_font_montserrat_*, which are switched off in lv_conf.h so the flash is not paid twice (the themes' default font is the 14 too). The metrics profiles point at them (neupod_font_14 and so on).

Font Characters 12, 14, 16, 20, 28 ASCII (U+0020 to 007E), Latin-1 (U+00A0 to 00FF, without the soft hyphen), bullet, en and em dash, curly single and double quotes, ellipsis, euro, and the 7 symbols still drawn from the fonts 48 ASCII and the note symbol only (the splash wordmark and the art-less note; it never shows a name)

Latin-1 covers the accented letters of Western European names (é ü ñ ø å ß ...) and ¿ ¡: some rippers write ¿ where the title had a ?, and it is a real glyph here. Line heights and baselines are set back to the built-in Montserrat values (the generator would otherwise grow every line by 2 to 5 px for the accented capitals), so every profile's layout is unchanged; an accent on a capital may reach a pixel or two above the line box.

Display-text filter. ui_text_display() (ui_logic.c, host-tested) turns a raw UTF-8 string into what the fonts can draw, so nothing renders as an empty box. It keeps every character the fonts have (ui_text_has_glyph() is that list, and a host test checks it against the compiled fonts) and maps the rest: combining accents and zero-width marks are dropped (a name stored as e plus a combining acute shows as e), other control characters and odd spaces become a space (a \n is kept for the multi-line panes), other dashes, quotes and the minus sign become their ASCII look-alikes, Latin Extended-A letters become the base letter (Ł to L, Œ to OE), fullwidth forms become ASCII, and anything else (CJK, Cyrillic, emoji) becomes one ? per character. Malformed UTF-8 becomes ?; a sequence cut off at the end of the string is dropped. The result is never longer than the input and the copy is cut only at a character boundary. Stored names and tags are never changed: the filter runs only on the way to a label, so a file is still found and opened by its real name.

ui_label_set_text() (ui_frame.c) applies it: it is how a label gets text from a file name, a tag, a device name or a network name, and it leaves the label alone when the result is what it already shows. Everything drawn from such a string goes through it: the Files and library rows (and their detail text), the screen titles (a folder name), Now Playing title, artist and album, the Home screen's playing lines, the toasts, the Settings panes (Bluetooth and Wi-Fi names) and the Bluetooth and Wi-Fi lists. Text the wheel keyboards build is typed from their own character sets and drawn as is. New code that puts a media string into a label must use it, and a new LV_SYMBOL_* needs its code point in tools/gen_ui_fonts.sh and ui_text_has_glyph(). Lucide icons are drawn with ui_icon() (an icon-font label, never run through the filter).

Flash cost on the RP2350 (Release): see the CHANGELOG entry for UI-17.

docs.title: Design system (2026-11-12 review)
docs.text:
From the owner-commissioned design review; phase 1 (the foundation, backlog DS-1 to DS-7 and HL-1, see Backlog) is built. The decisions the owner took where the review conflicted with earlier ones are in the README of the review and apply to every phase (Now Playing: Select opens page 2, hold Select seeks; a lost Bluetooth link stays paused on Bluetooth, ADR-0019; Light by default; the Pico 2 W is frozen; every third-party asset goes into LICENSE.md and the Licences screen).

Colour tokens and themes (DS-1). Every colour the UI draws is one of 14 tokens (ui_theme.h: bg, surface, bar, line, ink, ink2, ink3, accent, on_accent, accent_soft, amber, amber_soft, green, red), each with a Light and a Dark value from the review (RGB565-safe: red and blue multiples of 8, green of 4; test_ui_metrics checks it and the text contrast). Code names a token (UI_C_INK), never a hex value: labels, backgrounds and borders use shared styles that read the active theme (ui_style_text(), ui_obj_bg() ...), so switching rewrites those styles and restyles everything at once (one full repaint). The boot splash keeps its own fixed palette, and the art placeholder is not themed. Settings > Display > Theme is Light (default), Dark or Auto and is stored (SETTING_THEME, NPth); Auto is dark exactly while the backlight is dimmed or off (ui_theme_is_dark()), so with Auto-dim off it behaves like Light until the screen goes off (owner decision), switched before the backlight comes back on a wake. Contrast: the dark theme's white-on-accent is 4.2:1 (below 4.5:1) and the light one 6.4:1 (the review quotes 7.3:1).

Type scale (DS-2). Title = the large font (20 / 28), Body = 14 / 20, Small = 12 / 16 (secondary lines, times, pills, hints, the status bar's left slot; built from the same Montserrat Medium and the same glyph coverage), Big = 48.

Text that does not fit (ticker). Owner decision: one-line text wider than its box scrolls round instead of ending in dots, and a one-line label is always one line high (a dotted or scrolling label with a taller box would wrap). ui_label_ticker(label, on) (ui_frame.c) switches a label between dots and LVGL's circular scroll: 1 s pause, then ticker_px_s (35 px/s, 52 at 480x360) with a gap of three spaces between repeats, only while the text overflows. Used for the Home track title and artist, the focused list row's main text (style_row; the other rows keep dots and the label goes back to dots, rewound, when focus leaves) and the status-bar title. Only the label's own box is invalidated per frame. At most eight tickers exist at once. ui_ticker_set_active(false) (screen off) parks every ticker; ui_frame_settle() rewinds them, so snapshots always show the start position. Rule for later phases: Now Playing title, artist and album use it. Tour: text-home (Home with a long title and artist) and text-longrow (a focused Files row that is too long), ctest text_tour / hires_text_tour; the layout audit fails a dotted or ticker label whose box is two lines high.

Metrics. Status bar 24 / 36, row 30 / 45 (7 rows in both profiles), padding 10 / 15, selection bar inset 3 / 4 and radius 4 / 6, Home and Settings split 56 / 44, scroll bar 2 px wide with a track, toast strip one row high (30 / 45), HUD strip 26 / 39, lock pill 24 / 36, Power-hold line 3 / 4 (all in ui_metrics_t).

Status bar (DS-3). Left slot (Small, ink2), centred title, right-hand group (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, lock, battery percentage, battery; hidden members close up). The slot belongs to the screen on top: ui_screen_set_left(screen, text) (the text is kept with the screen, so a pop restores it). Built so far: the clock on Home, "n of m" on Now Playing (while a queue plays), the item count on the Music lists, the path in Files (the title stays "Files"). The battery is drawn (outline, terminal, fill), never "--": the fill is ink, green while charging, red below 15 %, and the percentage shows only below 20 % or while charging. The Bluetooth icon is ink3 for a saved headset that is not connected, ink connected, accent streaming, hidden with no radio or no headset. (The three busy dots of a background library build are not drawn yet; the slot is the place.)

Selection bar (DS-4). One rounded bar, inset from the list edges, behind the rows (ui_list.c); the rows are transparent. It slides to an adjacent row in 80 ms; a move of more than three rows (a fast spin) and a new list jump without animation. The selected row's text, detail and chevron use on_accent, the rest ink / ink2 (greyed rows ink3).

Strips (DS-5, HL-1; ui_strips.c). ui_toast_show(text, WARN | INFO, ms): a one-line strip under the status bar (amber_soft for a problem, accent_soft for information), slides down from under the bar in 150 ms and out in 200 ms. The audio route's "Headset disconnected" / "Headset not connected", the Files notices ("Not a playable file", "Path too long") and the library's "Can't play" are toasts now (they were a banner over the first row and a row at the bottom). (There is no "Headphones unplugged" notice in the firmware.) ui_hud_show(label, pct, ms): the bottom strip (ink, Small text and a bar) for a value changing from any screen, 120 ms in, 1200 ms hold, 200 ms out, the fill follows in 60 ms; the volume HUD itself is NP-4 (phase 2). ui_pill_show() / ui_hold_line_set(): the lock pill and the Power-hold line (see Hold). None of them dims or blends anything behind it. The host tour tokens toast:warn:Text_with_underscores, toast:info:..., hud:Label:PCT, strips:off and theme:light|dark|auto drive them for --tour-design (ctest design_tour, hires_design_tour).

Icons (DS-6). The Lucide set (ISC; chevron-right and lock derive from Feather, MIT) as 1-bit bitmaps at 16 / 24 px (320x240) and 24 / 36 px (480x360): chevron-right, play, pause, skip-back, skip-forward, shuffle, repeat, repeat-1, volume-2, bluetooth, wifi, lock, folder, file, lock-open, and the boot splash's check icons monitor, hard-drive, battery-medium, vibrate and circle-dot (ui_icons.h). They are generated from the pinned lucide-static package by tools/gen_ui_fonts.sh into neupod_icons_*.c and drawn with ui_icon() like a label, so they take a theme colour. Lists use the chevron, the Files rows the folder and file icons (ui_list_item_t.icon), the status bar Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and lock, Now Playing play / pause / shuffle / repeat. Battery and signal bars stay drawn shapes (the splash's battery-gauge icon is the Lucide glyph). The licence text is app/ui/fonts/LICENSE-Lucide.txt.

Motion (DS-7). Push slides the new screen in 24 px over 120 ms (ease-out), pop slides the revealed screen in from the left over 100 ms; no alpha, only the content area repaints. (The review fades the popped screen out; the popped screen is destroyed at once, so the mirror slide is used.) LVGL runs at 30 fps (LV_DEF_REFR_PERIOD 33, lv_conf.h) on every build; the Y2 stays at 30 until a vsync'd framebuffer is confirmed there. A snapshot or the layout audit first settles any slide or strip in flight (ui_frame_settle()).

Phase 2 (NP-1 to NP-5, LB-1 to LB-3) is described under Now playing, Music lists and Now Playing art above. Layout numbers (320x240 / 480x360 = x1.5, ui_metrics_t): Now Playing art 112 at (10, 12) in the content area, text column at x 134, title y 10, artist y 40, album y 60, pills y 102 (18 px high), progress bar y 142 (4 px, 6 px in seek mode, knob 14), times y 152, volume strip y 190; two-line rows 40 px (title y 3, second line y 21); album header and page 2: art 64 at y 8, rule at y 76; letter tile 44 px at (w - 58, 14), rail from y 6 over 204 px. The tours --tour-seek (seek-volume, np-nowplaying, seek-mode, seek-scrub, seek-cancel, seek-go, np-page2, np-volume-hud, seek-mp3, seek-unavailable), --tour-library (lib-songs two-line, lib-volume-hud, lib-songs-fastscroll, lib-album with the header) and --tour-art snapshot the new screens at both resolutions with the layout audit on every one; the tour tokens sel:down / sel:up (with sleep:MS) hold Select, vol:N changes the volume from outside the screen and rail:hold / rail:release keep the fast-scroll overlay up for a snapshot.

docs.title: Implemented (stage 2: home menu)
docs.text:
Firmware screens in app/ui/ (LVGL, light theme as in the mock-ups above; all drawing is original). Rendering is partial (two 320x24 strip buffers at 320x240; see Resolution profiles); the list scrolls with one short animation, everything else is static. Nothing persists across a reboot yet (settings are RAM only).

Common frame. A status bar on every screen: title in the middle, battery icon and percentage on the right ("--" when the gauge failed its check; green with a charge symbol while charging, red at 15 % or less), and a play/pause glyph slot on the left (empty: nothing plays yet), then the Wi-Fi glyph and the Bluetooth glyph: grey = a headset is remembered but not connected, dark = connected, accent blue = streaming audio, hidden when Bluetooth is not up or no headset is remembered and nothing is connected (the bar is light, so the "connected" colour is the text colour and not white). A toast (the strip under the status bar, 3 s, on any screen): "Headset disconnected" when the headset goes away while playing (the player is paused at once, the position kept, and the output stays Bluetooth), "Headset not connected" when Play is pressed on the Bluetooth output with no headset. Menu goes back one screen (nothing at the top level), Select enters. Lists clamp at both ends (no wrap), the selection bar jumps and the list scrolls smoothly when the selection leaves the window; a thin scroll bar shows on long lists.

Scrolling. The wheel reports counts; 4 counts make one list step, and fast movement multiplies it (2x, 4x, 8x when many counts arrive within 150 ms; the constants UI_COUNTS_PER_STEP, UI_ACCEL_* are in app/include/runtime_config.h). Each testbed key press is exactly one step.

Screen What it does now Home Left list: Music, Podcasts, Photos, Extras, Settings, Shuffle Songs, Now Playing. Right pane follows the player (polled on every UI tick, and at once when Home comes back on top; the clock and card summary refresh twice a second). Playing a file: the 96 px art box shows the album art thumbnail (the note when there is none), then title (file name when there is no title tag), artist, and a play or pause symbol with the queue position (3 of 12, or just Playing / Paused without a queue; Finished once the last track has ended, and Error, Verifying or Verified for those player states, detail stays on Now Playing). Test tone: note, tone name, Test signal, play symbol. Nothing playing: the artwork placeholder, Nothing playing, the clock (--:-- until the time is set) and a card summary (type and size, or No card). Music Artists, Albums, Songs, Genres, Compilations, Playlists (None yet) and Update Library; the lists are described under Music lists. Shuffle Songs Plays the whole library shuffled, building the index first if there is none; Menu on Now Playing comes back to Home. Podcasts, Photos Placeholder screens saying what is missing. Now Playing Live: title, artist and album with track number from the file's tags (the file name if there is no title), a format badge such as FLAC 24/96, MP3 320k or ALAC 16/44.1, Playing / Paused / Finished or the error, elapsed and remaining time with a progress bar, and the volume with a level bar. The wheel is the volume (2 dB per step, starts at -30 dB; on the Bluetooth output with a headset that has absolute volume it is the headset's volume: the label reads Headset 62%, the bar is the same scale, a swipe on the headset's stem moves it, and a headset at 0 % shows Headset 0% with Playing - headset volume 0% on the status line; the software volume then sits at 0 dB, see Bluetooth); Select hands the wheel to seek (below) and back; Play pauses and resumes (Select no longer does), and on Finished (or after a FLAC MD5 check) plays the same file again from the start, with sound; Right / Left = next / previous track of the queue on a short press (acted on at release; Previous more than 3 s into a track restarts it; Next on the last track stops and the screen goes idle); holding Right / Left for 0.6 s fast-forwards / rewinds (10x: the bar and the times run ahead, the track jumps there when the key is released; it also ends by itself at the start or end of the track and after 30 s, and another key, the wheel or another screen opening drops it unapplied); with more than one track queued the status line reads Playing - 3 of 12; Menu goes back while the sound continues. Without anything playing it says Nothing playing. Play/Pause works on every screen, and so do Right / Left (next / previous track) while a queue is playing, on every screen that does not use them itself (the Files browser keeps Right for the MD5 check of a .flac, the Test tone screen and the sliders keep them for their values, text entry keeps them). Seek mode (WAV, ALAC, MP3, and FLAC with a seek table; other tracks answer Seek not available for 2 s and the wheel stays on volume; WAV, ALAC and FLAC land on the exact frame, an MP3 on a frame header found from the Xing or VBRI table or, for constant bit rate, the byte proportion, so within a frame for CBR and within about 1 % of the track for a VBR file, and the bar then shows where it really landed): the progress bar turns orange and the volume bar grey, the volume label becomes Seek 1:23, each wheel step moves the position by about 1/60 of the track (1 to 30 s, accelerated like list scrolling), the new position is applied 0.35 s after the wheel stops (the track restarts at that frame: a short mute, paused stays paused) and the wheel drops back to volume 3 s after the last turn. A scrub or hold is tied to the track it was made on: if another track starts first (gapless handoff, skip) it is dropped. A position at the very end is the end of the track (the queue moves on). Extras Files, Test tone. Extras, Test tone Three rows, each On / Off: 1 kHz tone, L/R ident (1 s left, then 1 s right) and Scale (C4 up to C5 and back, looping). Select starts or stops the highlighted one (starting one stops the other); Left / Right = volume; the screen shows the volume and the level reaching the DAC. Leaving the screen stops the sound. See Audio. Extras, Files Read-only browser of the card: folders first then files, alphabetical, hidden entries skipped (a name starting with a dot, or the FAT hidden / system attribute: System Volume Information, $RECYCLE.BIN; the host build has no such attribute, so only the dot rule applies there), size on the right, a chevron on folders. Select opens a folder, Menu goes up (at the root it leaves). Select on a .wav, .flac, .mp3 or .m4a (ALAC) plays it and opens Now Playing; the rest of that folder (playable files only, in the order shown, from the chosen one) is queued and plays on by itself, gaplessly when the rate matches; Right on a .flac verifies its MD5 without sound (see Audio). Other files show Not a playable file for 3 s; an AAC .m4a opens Now Playing with AAC not supported yet. At most 256 entries per folder are kept (... more (first 256 shown) row after them); names longer than 63 bytes are cut at a character boundary. Directory reads run in the storage task, so the screen shows Loading... and keeps responding; without a working card it says why (Storage unavailable: no card). Settings Two panes (groups left, live summary right). About: first row Licences (Select opens the list of third-party components and their licences; Select on one shows its licence and a short notice; kept in step with LICENSE.md by a test, see Licences below), then Diagnostics (Select opens a list: the result of every boot check, heap free, core 1 stack, audio blocks / underruns / jitter, and the Bluetooth link: codec, bitpool, bit rate, underruns, frames, drift trims), then version, build hash, platform and uptime. Display: Select opens a five-row list: Backlight (Select, then scroll adjusts it in 5 % steps, never below 5 %), Auto-dim (Select toggles On/Off, default On), Dim after (Select cycles 10 s / 15 s / 30 s / 1 min / 2 min / 5 min, default 30 s; greyed and inert while Auto-dim is Off), Screen off after (Select cycles Never / 15 s / 30 s / 1 min / 2 min / 3 min / 5 min, default 3 min; counted from the dim, or from the last input when Auto-dim is Off) and Auto-lock (Select toggles On/Off, default On: Hold turns on when the screen goes off, Hold); all saved on the card. After the idle time with no input the backlight steps down to 10 % (a set level below 10 % is left alone, idle never brightens); any input restores the set level at once and is delivered to the screen as normal. After the Screen off time the backlight goes fully off; the input that wakes it is not delivered to the screen (and with Hold on, nothing is). The idle clock starts when the menu appears. Click: Select cycles Haptic / Off today (default Haptic, which needs the haptic driver); Piezo and Both join the cycle once a piezo driver exists; saved on the card, and an older saved On/Off still reads as Haptic/Off. Haptics: Select opens a two-row list: Actuator (Select toggles ERM / LRA; a changed type calibrates itself) and Calibrate (Select runs the auto-calibration, about a second; shows Not needed / Not done / Running... / Done / Failed); see I2C peripherals. Gapless playback: Select toggles On/Off (default On); saved on the card; Off keeps the auto-advance but with the ordinary stop and start between tracks. Resume playing: Select toggles On/Off (default Off); saved on the card. Off: the last track comes back paused at its place. On: if the player was playing when it was last used, it plays on again at boot (if it was paused or stopped, it still comes back paused). Bluetooth (design review BT-1 to BT-3): the right pane names the remembered headset and its state (or "No headset saved"); Select opens a short page: Audio output (Select cycles Auto / Wired / Bluetooth, saved on the card; Auto = Bluetooth whenever a headset's stream is open, shown as "Auto: Bluetooth" while it is; Bluetooth makes Bluetooth the output at once, headset or not, and keeps it through a Disconnect; Wired never uses Bluetooth; changing the output while a track plays stops it, the place is kept, like Stop), Devices (chevron; the remembered headset's state, "None", or why the radio is not usable) and Absolute volume (greyed, read-only: Yes when the connected headset reports one, No, or "-" with no link; the firmware has no switch for it). There is no Bluetooth On / Off row: the radio drivers have no clean power-down (backlog). Devices starts a scan as it opens (not while audio is streaming: an inquiry would stutter it; then "Scan again" does it on request) and fills in live: the remembered headset first with its state on the right (Connected, Streaming, Saved, Pairing..., Connecting..., Reconnecting... with busy dots, No audio, Failed: reason), then the devices found (audio devices first, strongest first once the scan ends; phones and other non-audio devices are greyed and carry "(phone)", "(computer)", "(wearable)" or "(other)"), each with the monochrome three-bar signal (ink and line, no traffic-light colours), then Scan again (Stop scanning while it runs). While a scan runs a strip at the bottom says "Scanning" with four dots filling in ink3; the status bar's left slot counts what was found. Select on a found audio device pairs (Bluetooth): the scan stops, the row's right text becomes "Pairing..." with busy dots, then the device moves to the top as the remembered headset ("Connected", "Streaming") or the row says "Failed: "; Menu cancels a pairing (the next Menu leaves). One headset is remembered: with one already saved, Select on a found device asks "Replace with ?" (Select = replace, Menu = keep). A non-audio row answers with the toast "Not an audio device". Select on the remembered headset opens a small list: Connect (Disconnect while connected, Cancel while working; greyed while a scan runs) and Forget, which asks "Forget ?" (Select = Forget, Menu = Keep: a question screen, no row ever changes its own meaning). Renaming a headset is not offered. The link's life is told by toasts: " disconnected . reconnecting..." (warning) when a connected headset goes away, " connected" (info, 1.2 s) when the automatic reconnect gets it back, "Couldn't reconnect - paused" (warning) when the five minutes run out; playback stays paused on Bluetooth and the output is never switched by itself (ADR-0019). Names from the headset go through the display-text filter (Fonts and display text; the stored name is untouched); up to 48 bytes are kept. Wi-Fi: on/off, status (name, address, signal as a meter), Scan for networks (opens the Networks screen: it scans as it opens; first row Scan again, then the networks found and the remembered ones, a name with * is remembered; each name once, with its strongest access point; Select on one starts the join flow, Menu goes back), Other network..., time zone, the time (set by hand if there is no network), Wi-Fi while playing; see Wi-Fi. Storage: card type, size, filesystem, mode, free space (computed by the storage task, computing... until done). Battery: voltage, charge, rate, state, alerts, gauge status; live, once a second.

docs.title: Now Playing art
docs.text:
The 112 x 112 box (168 at 480x360) at the top left of Now Playing shows the album art of the track that is playing; page 2 and the album header show it at 64 / 96 px.

Thumbnails and cache (NP-5). Hosted builds (the simulator and the Y2; NEUPOD_ART_HIRES, on by default there) decode to a 160 x 160 RGB565 thumbnail (50 KB) and keep the last 24 albums (1.2 MB static: 24 slots, least recently used replaced first, the slots on screen are never replaced); nothing is scaled up: LVGL draws the thumbnail smaller into the box (160 to 112, 96, 64), except Now Playing at 480x360 where the 168 px box shows it 5 % larger. The cache key is the one that already identified an album (folder, album tag, embedded picture size), so a track of an album played or browsed before shows its art at once. The Pico 2 W build (frozen, ADR-0001 amendment) keeps the 64 x 64 thumbnail (8 KB), no cache and no browse art (ART_CACHE_N 1, art.h); an RP2350B with PSRAM turns the large thumbnails on with -DNEUPOD_ART_HIRES=ON. Measured RAM: 24 x 51,200 B = 1,228,800 B of BSS on the host and the Y2 (the Y2 has plenty); RP2350 unchanged. The album header asks the art service for the album's picture by the library handle of its first song (art_browse_want()): the storage task resolves it, reads the file's header for an embedded picture, and decodes it into the cache when it is idle (the playing track's art always goes first).

(The table and text below describe the decoder, written for the 64 px thumbnail.)

State What the box shows Track just started, art being found or decoded The dark box with a note glyph (the audio always starts first; art never delays it) JPEG found The picture, kept in proportion and centred, with the dark box as letterbox bars No art, PNG, progressive JPEG, damaged JPEG, picture too large (over 5120 px) The note glyph Nothing playing, a test tone, an error, or still opening The note glyph

Where the picture comes from, in order: the picture inside the file (MP3 ID3v2 APIC / PIC, FLAC PICTURE, MP4 covr; a JPEG is preferred to a PNG, a front cover to other types), then cover.jpg, folder.jpg, front.jpg in the track's folder (any letter case; that order). An embedded PNG is skipped without being read, and the folder is then tried. A JPEG that is embedded but progressive or damaged also falls back to the folder files. PNG and progressive JPEG need the PSRAM board (ADR-0013, amendment of 3 Nov 2026).

How it works: after the track has started, the storage task (core 0, the only user of the card) decodes the JPEG with TJpgDec straight from the card in 512-byte reads, shrunk by the decoder to 1/1, 1/2, 1/4 or 1/8 (the largest shrink that keeps the long side at 64 pixels or more), one MCU row at a time, and averages it into one 64 x 64 RGB565 thumbnail (8 KB of static RAM); the whole picture is never in RAM. LVGL shows the thumbnail scaled to fit the box (1.75 times for a full-size thumbnail; soft edges are the price of the RAM). While it decodes, the task keeps the audio data ring topped up, sleeps 1 ms after every 2 ms of work (so input and UI keep running, the storage task outranks them) and stops as soon as another request is queued (it restarts afterwards). The result is kept for the album: a track whose folder, album tag and embedded picture size match the last one shows it at once, without decoding again. A big picture takes roughly a second or two on the bench (the card read dominates); the art: line on the UART gives source, size, scale and time. Decoder working memory (about 8.6 KB at most) comes from the heap for the length of one decode; if it is not available the note stays. Colour order: the thumbnail is native-order RGB565 like LVGL's draw buffers (the display driver swaps for the panel).

Click feedback. Every list step asks the haptic task for a click (ROM effect 3, a gentle click). The request is a non-blocking queue write: the UI never waits on the I2C bus, requests closer than 35 ms are dropped, and the driver goes back to standby after 2 s without a click or at any error.

Keys. UART testbed: w/k up, s/j down, Enter or e Select, m or Backspace Menu, a Left, d Right, p or Space Play/Pause. Host window: Up/Down arrows and mouse wheel scroll, Enter Select, Esc/Backspace/m Menu, Left/Right, Space/p Play/Pause. The wheel, when it works, sends the same events.

Signal meter and busy dots. Wi-Fi network rows and the Wi-Fi status row show signal as four small bars at the right edge instead of dBm (Bluetooth device rows use the monochrome three-bar meter, ui_list_item_t.mono: ink bars on line-grey, ui_signal_bars3() folds the four levels to three, no colour): 4 or 3 bars green, 2 yellow, 1 red (the unlit bars are grey). Wi-Fi: 4 bars at -60 dBm or stronger, 3 down to -70, 2 down to -80, else 1; Bluetooth is 5 dB stronger (-55 / -65 / -75). The thresholds and the 3 dB hysteresis are UI_SIG_* in runtime_config.h; ui_signal_bars() (ui_logic.c, host-tested in test_ui_logic) is a pure function. The Wi-Fi icon in the status bar takes the colour of the joined network's bars and changes only after the signal has moved 3 dB past a threshold, so it does not flicker. A list row whose action is still running (a join started from the Networks list, a Wi-Fi or Bluetooth scan, the radio starting) shows four pulsing dots in the same place: set busy on the row in the list model (ui_list_item_t, alongside bars) for as long as the work lasts and call ui_list_refresh when it changes; the list animates it with one timer that runs only while a visible row is busy. The model owns the end: a Networks join ends when the station is up, the join fails, or UI_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS (the join deadline) passes.

Console log (UART). Every screen push and pop prints ui: screen 'Title' push|pop [-> 'Revealed'] depth=N lvgl_mem=used/totalB (modals too), and every list step prints ui: sel <screen> <index> '<label>', so the UI can be driven with the testbed keys without seeing the panel. Passwords are never printed: the text widget is not a list.

Host tour. neupod --tour --snapshots DIR walks through the screens by script and writes home, music-menu, music-empty, extras, files, files-sub, files-many, files-many-end, settings, settings-bt, bt-idle, bt-scanning and bt-found (the Devices screen), bt-pair, about, nowplaying (PPM) into DIR (the tour's key script predates the longer Settings list, so several of these names no longer show the screen they are named for; use --tour-bt for Bluetooth); neupod --tour-bt --snapshots DIR walks the Bluetooth screens and writes settings-bt (the Settings pane), settings-lineout and settings-speaker (the two toggle rows before Bluetooth: Settings > Speaker On / Off and Line out On / Off, grey with Plug into the jack first / None when unavailable), bt-output-speaker (Audio output cycles Auto, Wired, Bluetooth, Speaker; the toast Speaker is off: turn it on in Settings), bt-idle (Settings > Bluetooth), bt-output-bt (Audio output set to Bluetooth), bt-scanning (Devices with the four dots), bt-found, bt-pairing (the row's "Pairing..." with busy dots), bt-paired (the headset on top, Connected), bt-options (Disconnect / Forget), bt-forget-asks and bt-replace-asks (the question screens), bt-disconnected (Saved), bt-forgotten, bt-failed (a pairing the simulated car kit refuses), then the audio half on a card with a 20 s WAV album: np-bt-badge (Now Playing, SBC 44.1), np-bt-volume, np-bt-volume0, bt-key-next, bt-about and bt-diag (About with Diagnostics, and the Diagnostics list scrolled to the Bluetooth link rows), bt-streaming (Devices: Streaming, no scan started), settings-bt-streaming, bt-dropped (the bt:drop token makes the simulated headset vanish: the toast "... disconnected . reconnecting...", the player paused), bt-reconnected (the info toast, about 2.5 s later) and bt-gave-up (the give-up toast, set with the toast: token: the five minutes are not simulated); ctest bt_tour and, at 480x360 with the layout audit, hires_bt_tour; neupod --tour-art --snapshots DIR plays three one-track albums (cover file, JPEG inside the FLAC, PNG inside plus a progressive cover) and writes art-cover, art-embedded, art-none (ctest art_tour, checked by art_snapshot). neupod --tour-text --snapshots DIR (UI-17) walks Extras > Files on a card with accented, ¿, curly-quote, CJK and emoji names (tests/tools/make_text_card.py) and plays a FLAC with accented tags: text-files, text-folder, text-nowplaying, text-home (Home with the long accented title: one line, ending in dots) (ctest text_tour and hires_text_tour); ctest runs it as runtime_smoke against a small fixture card (build/host/fsroot_fixture, NEUPOD_FS_ROOT) and writes build/host/snapshots/.

docs.title: Phase 4 (built part): library states, Settings pane, Home
docs.text:
Full-pane states (LB-4, ui_pane.c). A state with no rows covers the list: heading (Title font), up to two Small lines, a bar with a Small caption, an accent button naming what Select does, and a hint line at the bottom. ui_library.c uses it for opening (shown only after 300 ms), building, an error (with "Try again"), the Update Library result ("Done") and an empty list ("No artists yet", "Update Library"). "Library needs a writable card" is also a toast. Determinate progress: the build first counts the audio files (directory entries only, same filters as the scan; Cancel works during the count), so the bar is files / total and the caption reads "552 of 1,204 songs . Aurora Lane" (folder name from the scan). Run in background: Menu on the build pane leaves the screen, the build carries on and the status bar's left slot shows three busy dots on every screen; a toast says how it ended ("Library updated . 1,204 songs", or "Library update stopped" if the card was wanted for something else: any other card request, e.g. Play, still ends a build, the old index stands). Opening Update Library while one runs in the background takes it over. Greyed songs (LB-5): the codec at the right of a greyed two-line row (an album track already showed it in brackets); a queue that skips an unplayable track toasts "Skipped: unsupported codec (AAC)" (player_skip_notice). ui_frame_push returns false when the stack is full; Go to album / artist then toast "Can't open: too many screens".

Settings (ST-1, ST-2). The right pane is a left-aligned summary: group name (Body), up to four key / value lines (Small, key ink2, value ink right-aligned) and one help line (Small, ink3). Gapless, Shuffle, Repeat, Resume and Click change in place on Select with a haptic tick and a 60 ms flip of the value in the pane. Settings > Display is Theme, Brightness (the slider), Dim after (10 s to 5 min, then Off: that is Auto-dim), Off after, Auto-lock.

Home (3.1). Playing: art, title and artist (tickers), a 3 px progress bar, elapsed (pause glyph in front when paused) and remaining. Idle: the clock at 48 px and the date once the clock is set (otherwise "Nothing playing"), then "1,204 songs . 72 %" (one Info request for the song count when the panel goes idle; "No library yet" and "Open Music to build it" when there is no index). "Now Playing" is greyed while nothing is queued (Select says "Nothing playing"); Shuffle Songs has no chevron. The card summary line ("SDHC 32 GB") exists only with -DNEUPOD_UI_DEBUG=ON.

docs.title: Playlists (phase 4b, LB-7)
docs.text: Music > Playlists (ui_playlists.c, over playlist_service.h on the storage task; not on the frozen Pico 2 W, where the row still says None yet). The list of lists: On-The-Go, Recently added, Most played, Top rated, Unplayed, then every .m3u / .m3u8 found in /, /Playlists and /Music, each with its count at the right (128+ where the count is a floor). Select opens a list as two-line rows (title, then artist or folder); Select on a song plays the whole list from it (player_play_paths: the queue holds whole paths, Shuffle and Repeat apply). A row the card cannot play (file missing, path that is not on the card, not a music file) is greyed with the reason on its second line and answers Select with a toast. Empty lists, loading and errors are full-pane layouts like the library's. Entries are read like a player would: #EXTM3U / #EXTINF, relative and absolute paths, Windows separators and drive letters, file://, byte-order mark, Latin-1 or UTF-8 (pl_m3u.h). Smart lists: Recently added = the 50 newest files by modified time (one pass over the index), Most played = the 25 with most counted plays, Top rated = four stars or more, Unplayed = library songs with no counted play, in title order, the first 128. On-The-Go: Now Playing page 2 > Add to On-The-Go (toast Added to On-The-Go, Already in On-The-Go, or why not); in the list a long press of Select (0.5 s) takes the song off, and a last row Clear On-The-Go asks first. Files and formats: Storage. Tour --tour-playlists (ctest playlists_tour, hires_playlists_tour; snapshots pl-*).

docs.title: Cover Flow (phase 4c, LB-6)
docs.text: On the Albums list, Right turns the list into five flat album tiles (centre 96 px, neighbours 64, outer 48 at 320x240; 144 / 96 / 72 at 480x360; no rotation or reflection; the nearer tile overlaps the farther by a few pixels). Under the centre tile: the title (Body, ticker if long) and Artist . 2019 . 3 songs (Small, ink2, ticker). The status bar's left slot reads 7 of 31. The wheel moves one album per detent (up to three when it spins fast); a single step slides the tiles over 90 ms (size and position only, the tile row is the only area redrawn), a jump just moves them. Play plays the album from its first song, Select opens it, Left or Right goes back to the list on the same album. Placeholder tiles (the art-less gradient) show until a picture arrives. ui_coverflow.c holds the tiles: seven tile objects as a ring (the tile of album a is tile a mod 7, so a step only moves geometry), each an image that points straight at the art service's thumbnail (not copied). ui_library.c owns the data and frees the list's rows while the flow shows (the list keeps its selection). Albums rows carry first, songs and year (the year of the first song) for this (lvw_row_t). The year is missing from the subtitle for an album whose first song has none. Art service (art_service.h): art_browse_want_set() takes up to ART_BROWSE_N (5) library handles, centre first; the storage task decodes them in that order into the existing 24-slot cache (a cache hit by album key costs one file header read; a handle already cached costs nothing, so a step decodes only the one new tile). Wanted handles, and the set wanted just before, are never evicted; art_browse_get_handle() answers by handle (READY / LOADING / FAILED / NONE) under the same retry counter as the playing track's view. A decode in progress is abandoned only when its handle is no longer wanted, so a wheel that never rests does not starve the tiles it passes. The art lookup uses library_service_resolve_for_art(), which does not take the place of a playing track's path in the resume cache and also finds the picture of a track the player cannot play. Compiled out where there is no art cache (NEUPOD_ART_HIRES off: the frozen Pico 2 W; Right then keeps its usual meaning). Tour: lib-coverflow, lib-coverflow-next, lib-coverflow-far, lib-coverflow-start, lib-coverflow-back in --tour-library.

docs.title: Text entry, number, slider, date / time (phase 4c, IN-1, IN-2)
docs.text: Described in Input widgets: the letter ring with mode chips, the password reveal (800 ms), hold Menu to clear, the Big value with the bar and its min / max, the date / time field names. The Wi-Fi password and name, Test URL and the search use the same modal; the request API (wi_request_t) is unchanged, the model lost its cursor, page, show and done keys (wheel_input.h). Tour --tour-input: in-text, in-text-123, in-text-space, in-text-del, in-text-cleared, in-password, in-password-dots, ...

docs.title: Files, long folders (phase 4c, FL-1)
docs.text: A folder with more than 256 entries (FILES_MAX_ENTRIES) is read a page at a time (storage_list_request_page(): the page is the entries 256 * n onwards in the order directories then files, each page sorted by name on its own). The list ends in a plain Load more row (it replaces the old greyed "... more" row) that shows the next page; a later page starts with Earlier entries. A folder found to hold more than a page shows 256+ at the right of its row when its parent is listed again (it is learnt on opening: the folders are not counted before). Icons (folder / file) and the path in the status bar's left slot were built in phase 1 (/, /Name, .../Name). Tour: files-page2, files-page1-end, files-plus.

docs.title: Splash (phase 4c, SP-1)
docs.text: The release splash is the wordmark, the progress line (the shimmer under it), the icon row and the version in the dim ink, shown at least 600 ms (RT_SPLASH_MIN_MS). The icon row has one Lucide icon per boot check (Display = monitor, Storage = hard-drive, Battery gauge = battery-medium, Haptics = vibrate, Click wheel = circle-dot, Audio = volume-2, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi), in a 32 px box (48 px at 480x360) at y = 116 (174): the icon pulses while its check runs, goes solid with an accent border when it passes and gets a red cross when the subsystem is not fully correct. The icon row was reinstated at the owner's request on 2026-11-13 (Y2 test: "I want the icons back, that loading screen was good"); the first SP-1 cut had replaced it with text. The debug splash keeps the icons and adds a short text list under them when a boot check ended not fully correct, or when Menu is held while the unit starts: one red line per failed check (Battery gauge - no response, with +n more if they do not fit), then 6 of 8 checks passed (All 8 checks passed when Menu was held and nothing failed); the bar along the bottom drains over the 8 s hold (any other key skips it). Keys pressed while the splash shows go to the home screen afterwards. The red caption under the icons is gone (the debug list replaces it); the list has room for three lines at both sizes (test_ui_metrics pins it). Host: --splash-debug / --splash-release; ctest splash_* and hires_splash_*.

docs.title: Not yet drawn
docs.text:
• Hold-switch lock overlay, charging screen, USB mass-storage ("Connected") screen.
  • Podcasts and Photos browsers; the search screen.

docs.title: Hold
docs.text:
Decision: ADR-0020. Hold is the iPod's lock switch, on every platform. While it is on, the wheel and every button do nothing: ui_frame_input() swallows them before any screen sees them (so there is no click, no Play/Pause, no scroll), and each one only restarts the idle clock and shows the lock pill ("Locked · hold Power 2 s to unlock"). Headset buttons (AVRCP) keep working; the Y2's side volume keys are locked with the rest. A lock icon sits in the status bar's right-hand group while Hold is on.

What How Auto-lock the screen goes fully off (Screen off after, or a Power tap) and Settings > Display > Auto-lock is On Gesture Power held 2 s toggles Hold: from 0.4 s a 3 px accent line grows under the status bar and a dark pill at the bottom says "Keep holding to lock · 10 s = off" (or "... to unlock"; letting go early does nothing), at 2 s the pill says "Locked" / "Unlocked" and a haptic click plays Power-off still held: at 5 s the line turns red and grows again while the pill counts "Release to cancel · shutting down in 5 ... 1" (letting go cancels), at 10 s the power-off is requested (Y2; the Pico rig cannot, and shows no countdown) Tap Power tapped (under 0.4 s) turns the screen off now; the next input wakes it (and is lost) Switch the iPod 6G donor board's slide switch (hal_input_hold_switch()), same state; none on the Y2 or the Pico rig Console / simulator no Power key on the Pico rig: the console key l toggles Hold. Simulator: F1 is Power (hold it)

The reminder ("Locked · hold Power 2 s to unlock"), the confirmations and the countdown are the lock pill and the Power-hold line of the design system (ui_strips.c; HL-1): nothing is dimmed, blended or covered except the pill itself. They are drawn at both UI profiles and covered by the layout audit (hold_tour, hires_hold_tour: ring, locked, swallowed keys, countdown, power-off, switch, screen off, wake, unlock, the Display rows).

docs.title: Licences
docs.text: Settings > About > Licences lists the third-party parts of the firmware and their licences (app/ui/ui_licence_data.c): the neuPod licences, FreeRTOS, LVGL, Montserrat, Lucide, Font Awesome, FatFs, TJpgDec, dr_flac / dr_mp3, Apple Lossless, mbed TLS, BTstack (with the non-commercial note), the Android SBC codec and, on the RP2350 build only, lwIP, cyw43-driver, the SD card driver and the Pico SDK. Select on a row shows the licence as a headline and a short plain notice (no scrolling: at most 400 characters). The table is the on-device copy of the one in LICENSE.md; ctest -R licences fails if a component is listed on the device but not named, with its licence, in LICENSE.md. Adding a dependency means adding it to both.

docs.title: Wi-Fi: lwIP, the Wi-Fi service, the clock and secrets at rest
docs.text: Stage W1 of the Wi-Fi work (ADR-0007 keeps the radio behind hal_radio.h). Bluetooth is described in Bluetooth; the on-screen keyboard in Wheel input widgets. Not on the board yet: everything here was built and tested on the PC and compiled for the RP2350.

docs.title: Stack and memory
docs.text:
• The CYW43 arch is now the SDK's lwIP + FreeRTOS variant (pico_cyw43_arch_lwip_sys_freertos). BTstack is unchanged and still runs on the same async context (the radio worker task): cyw43_arch_init() starts the driver, lwIP, then BTstack, in that order. IPv4 only, no sockets, no TLS.
  • platforms/rp2350/lwip/lwipopts.h: static pools only (MEM_LIBC_MALLOC off), MEM_SIZE 6000, 12 pbufs, TCP window 4 x 1460, 16 TCP segments, 4 TCP and UDP control blocks. lwIP callbacks (DHCP, DNS, SNTP, HTTP) run on lwIP's own tcpip thread (priority 3, 2 KB stack on the heap (lwIP's FreeRTOS port takes the size in bytes; 1 KB left only 312 B free after a join on the bench)), not on the CYW43 worker; the SDK's FreeRTOS arch serialises the two with the async-context lock. Both, and the wifi task, appear in the monitor's per-task stack-free line, which is the number to watch. Country code GB (channels 1 to 13).
  • Cost (arm-none-eabi-size, whole firmware): static RAM 436,480 B (end of the Bluetooth work) to 476,968 B, +40.5 KB (after the review fixes: 32 settings tags and a second staging array, +3.4 KB), of which lwIP is about 28.9 KB (pbuf pool 18.4 KB, memory heap 6 KB, TCP and the rest), mbed TLS and the secrets code about 2.5 KB (arena 2 KB), larger settings tables about 2 KB, the rest the Wi-Fi service and UI. Flash 1,120,532 B to 1,214,268 B, +94 KB: lwIP, the HTTP client, mbed TLS (AES-GCM, SHA-256, HKDF), the CYW43 Wi-Fi code, the Wi-Fi service, the UI widgets. The heap is not measured on the board yet: new heap users are the tcpip thread (2 KB stack), the "wifi" task (4 KB), and sockets-less lwIP objects; the radio worker is unchanged at 6 KB (RT_STACK_RADIO, checked against CYW43_TASK_STACK_SIZE at compile time). Stack overflow checking is on (configCHECK_FOR_STACK_OVERFLOW 2). The monitor prints heap: free= min_free= every 10 s; compare with the Bluetooth figures.

docs.title: The Wi-Fi service (app/runtime/wifi_service.c)
docs.text:
One task, "wifi" (core 0, priority 1, 4 KB stack), owns the station side. It runs every 200 ms and handles requests from the UI (a queue, never blocking the UI).

Feature How scan hal_wifi_scan_*: SSID, RSSI, channel, security; one UART line per access point from the radio (wifi: bss 'ssid' aa:bb:.. rssi=-48 ch=6 auth_bits=0x05), one per network after merging (wifi: scan: 'ssid' rssi=-48 sec=WPA2 ch=6, strongest access point wins; never any password) and wifi: scan done, N networks. Names in log lines are printable ASCII only (anything else shows as ?). The driver reports only three bits (4 = RSN element, 2 = WPA element, 1 = privacy) and cannot tell WPA3 from WPA2 (both carry an RSN element), so an RSN network shows "WPA2" (the join still tries WPA2, WPA2/WPA3 and WPA3-only in turn), WPA1-only and WEP show "secured" (wifi_sec_from_scan_bits, host tested); a scan that the user walked away from (Menu on Networks) is finished by the radio by itself, and a new scan waits up to 8 s for the radio to be free instead of showing an empty list; hidden networks do not appear and are added with "Other network..." join WPA2-PSK, WPA2/WPA3 mixed and WPA3-SAE, open networks. The cyw43 driver supports all three; a join tries WPA2, then mixed, then WPA3-only, moving on when an attempt fails. Wrong password is reported as such and is not retried in a loop DHCP, DNS lwIP SNTP lwIP's client, default pool.ntp.org (setting NPns), resynchronises about hourly; the answer sets the wall clock remembered networks up to 4. SSID and a "has password" flag in the clear, the password sealed (see below). "Forget" in the network's action menu join deadline a join still "joining" or "no address" 60 s after it started (RT_WIFI_JOIN_TIMEOUT_MS, wifi_join_timed_out() host tested, wrap-safe) is abandoned: hal_wifi_abort_join() leaves the network, the service logs wifi: join 'ssid' timed out (no IP after 60 s) and counts a real failure, so the normal backoff and auto-join retry. The state shows as failed (not "wrong password"), also for a join the user started. Found on the bench: after a reset the radio sat in "joined, no address" for over 10 minutes; on a marginal link (−80 dBm and below) DHCP OFFER/ACK frames are lost and the exchange can take 20–40 s, hence 60 s. DHCP is started once when the station interface is created (cyw43 dhcp_start) and lwIP restarts it on every link-up; the HAL does not restart it per join reconnect after a failure or a lost link: 2, 4, 8 ... up to 120 s between attempts (wifi_backoff_t, host tested); a user request or a success resets it; saved networks are tried in turn. With nothing saved nothing is attempted: the service only looks again every 10 s, and that is not counted as a failure (failures= counts real join failures and lost links) power wifi_policy_decide(): Wi-Fi is off while audio plays unless "Wi-Fi while playing" is On (default Off); the station is switched off after N idle minutes (default 10; setting); a scan, join, transfer or NTP resync counts as a need. The radio is shared with Bluetooth, and audio comes first diagnostics UART line every 10 s: wifi: state=up ssid=.. rssi=.. ip=.. ntp=1 saved=n reconnects=n failures=n lwip mem=used/size (max) pbuf=used/size (max) errs=n; Extras > Network test

The radio is switched with hal_wifi_start() / hal_wifi_stop(). hal_wifi_stop means "radio idle": the station interface is taken down (netif removed, link left) but the CYW43 chip itself stays powered, because Bluetooth runs on it; it is not a WLAN power-down and saves less current than the name suggests (measure it).

Settings stored: NPwf (enabled, during playback, idle minutes, zone), NPns (NTP server), NPtu (test URL), NPn0..3 (SSID records), NPp0..3 (sealed passwords).

docs.title: Coexistence with Bluetooth and audio
docs.text: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth share the CYW43439 and its bus, and lwIP, BTstack and the driver share the radio worker task. Mitigations: Wi-Fi is off during playback by default (the radio is then free for Bluetooth audio in stage 2); BTstack's controller flow control settings (btstack_config.h) limit what is in flight; the worker has a 6 KB stack. Core 1 (audio) never touches any of this. What to measure on the board: Bluetooth scan while joined, an HTTP transfer while a file plays (audio: underruns=), and the effect of "Wi-Fi while playing = On".

docs.title: The clock (app/net/sys_clock.c)
docs.text: hal_millis() stays the monotonic time for audio and timeouts. The wall clock is UTC (from SNTP, or set by hand in Settings > Wi-Fi > Time) as an offset from it. There is no time zone database: a zone is a base UTC offset plus "follows the EU rule". Presets: UTC, London (GMT/BST, the default), Central Europe (+1), Eastern Europe (+2). The EU rule: summer time runs from 01:00 UTC on the last Sunday of March to 01:00 UTC on the last Sunday of October. Tests check both edges to the second for 2024 to 2027 (ctest -R wifi_logic). The home pane shows HH:MM Mon 2 Nov once the time is known and --:-- before. There is no battery-backed RTC: after a power cycle the clock is unknown until the next NTP answer.

docs.title: Boot check and status icon
docs.text: The "wifi" boot check is ok when the radio driver and lwIP are up, not when a network is joined. A degraded check means the driver itself failed. "No network saved" is shown in Settings > Wi-Fi (status row and the right-hand pane), not as a boot failure. The status bar shows a Wi-Fi symbol: hidden when the station is off, grey while idle or connecting, green when up, red after a failure.

docs.title: Secrets at rest
docs.text:
What is stored: Wi-Fi passwords and Bluetooth link keys (and any later secret). How:

  • AES-256-GCM from the Pico SDK's mbed TLS 3.6 (Apache-2.0 option of its Apache-2.0 / GPL-2.0-or-later licence). Chosen over BTstack's rijndael because that is AES block encryption only: GCM (authenticated encryption) would have meant writing our own mode, which is the wrong thing to hand-roll. Only aes, gcm, cipher, sha256, md, hkdf and support files are compiled, with our own configuration (app/crypto/neupod_mbedtls_config.h), about 10 KB of flash, and a 2 KB static arena as its allocator.
  • Key: key_provider_get() (app/crypto/key_provider_chipid.c) returns a 32-byte key = HKDF-SHA-256 over the RP2350's 64-bit unique chip ID with a fixed application salt. The ID is the OTP chip ID read by the boot ROM before main (the SDK's pico_get_unique_board_id); it does not read the flash (on the RP2040 the same call talks to the flash chip, which would stall core 1; RP2350 does not). The host uses a fixed test ID. This is the only place that knows where the key comes from: moving to OTP or a secure element means replacing that one file.
  • Record: version byte, 12-byte random nonce (new for every write), ciphertext, 16-byte tag; the record's settings tag is the authenticated data, so a record cannot be copied to another tag. A password of up to 63 characters fits. Anything that does not authenticate (another neuPod, a card edited on a PC, damage) reads as absent: the Wi-Fi screen shows "password needed" and asks again, BTstack pairs again.
  • Existing plaintext Bluetooth link keys (from before encryption) are sealed on the first load. FAT does not scrub freed clusters, so the old plaintext may remain on the card in free space; the card is not safe for that old data.
  • Plaintext copies (the sealed value's plaintext, typed passwords in the keyboard widget and its result) are wiped after use.
  • NTP answers earlier than 2025-01-01 are rejected; the clock re-anchors hourly so the 49.7-day millisecond wrap is harmless.

docs.title: What this does NOT protect (read this)
docs.text:
The RP2350 has no EEPROM and no battery-backed NVRAM, and this firmware has no secure boot. The chip ID is not secret: it can be read with a debugger, and boards often show it as the USB serial number. So the encryption protects a lost or copied microSD card on its own; it does not protect against someone who has the card and the board (they can derive the same key). SSIDs are stored in the clear on purpose.

Production policy (design response, 3 Nov 2026; not built): on the RP2350 a random 256-bit key is written once to OTP at provisioning, using the OTP key page and page lock; the chip-ID HKDF above stays only as the pre-provisioning fallback. No secure element. An ESP32 / ESP32-S3 board uses an eFuse key and flash encryption under the same policy. Secure boot is a separate, later decision. All of this replaces key_provider_get() only. Writing OTP is irreversible: the provisioning step needs its own review before it runs on any board.

docs.title: Throughput test
docs.text: Extras > Network test: an HTTP GET (no TLS) of the URL in settings (default http://192.168.1.10:8000/test.bin, change it with Select on the URL row; serve a file with python3 -m http.server 8000 on the PC), body discarded, KB/s reported. It runs on the radio worker while audio plays, so the check is the audio: line. Not built: the variant that writes the download to an SD scratch file under /.neupod/tmp through the scoped write window (needs a ring between the radio worker and the storage task); today the target is discard only.

docs.title: Staged plan
docs.text:
Order (design response, 3 Nov 2026): W2 → W4 → W3. Library sync is why Wi-Fi exists, then OTA, then podcasts.

Stage Content W1 (done) lwIP, the Wi-Fi service, join/scan/forget with the wheel keyboard, SNTP and the clock, sealed secrets, diagnostics W2 (next) device HTTP API and a C# companion app for library sync (no TLS on the device) W4 over-the-air updates: bootrom A/B partitions with TBYB, image staged on SD, flashed only with playback stopped and core 1 parked in SRAM (ADR-0014) W3 podcasts through the companion; polish: roaming, AP list caching, captive portal detection, Wi-Fi during playback measurements, SD-file throughput test

docs.title: What to check on the board
docs.text:
1. Boot: boot: wifi ok : driver and lwIP up, bt: lines as before, Bluetooth still ok. Splash with both radios solid.
  2. Settings > Wi-Fi > Scan for networks (opens the Networks screen and scans at once): your networks appear with signal; Select your home network, type the password with the wheel (Select types, Menu deletes, the last key show unmasks, Play joins). The status shows the address and the signal; wifi: joined ... on the UART.
  3. NTP: the home screen shows the time (and the right zone, BST in summer) a few seconds after joining. Reboot: it is --:-- until the network is back.
  4. Power cycle: it reconnects by itself; the password is not asked again. Move the card to another board (or edit the file): "password needed".
  5. Play a file: the Wi-Fi symbol disappears (radio paused) unless "Wi-Fi while playing" is On. With it On, run the Network test and watch audio: for underruns=0.
  6. Settings > Bluetooth > Scan while joined: still finds the headset.
  7. Read heap:, lvgl_mem= and the wifi: line's lwIP figures after all that.

docs.title: Innioasis Y2 platform (NEUPOD_PLATFORM=y2)
docs.text: The same firmware as the host build (FreeRTOS tasks, LVGL UI, boot checks, player, FatFs storage), running as a Linux process on the Innioasis Y2 testbed (MT6582, armv7 hard-float, stock kernel 3.4.67, our Buildroot glibc rootfs). It is a testbed target for the UI and the library engine, not a product. Nothing here flashes the Y2: the firmware is copied into /opt over ssh. Background on the device itself is in testbed/y2/README.md.

docs.title: Where the code is
docs.text:
Path What platforms/y2/ the target: main.c, CMakeLists.txt, hal/ platforms/y2/hal/y2_*.c portable logic, also built and unit-tested on the PC: evdev decoding and the wheel mapping (y2_input), SD device selection (y2_sd), power_supply parsing (y2_power), the poweroff and reboot requests (y2_poweroff), boot-mode detection (y2_sysfs), charging-only mode logic (y2_charge) and its screen (y2_chargeview: the battery drawing and the screen-on timer), RGB565 to XRGB8888 and the page flipper (y2_fb), the wired audio path (y2_audio: allow-lists, S16 conversion, ring, DAC state machine) platforms/y2/hal/hal_*.c the HALs that touch the device (display, input, console, storage, battery, audio, radio, i2c, system) cmake/toolchain-y2.cmake the cross toolchain hal/host/freertos, hal/host/hal_core.c reused from the host build: the FreeRTOS POSIX port, and core 1 as a native thread tests/test_y2_*.c host unit tests (ctest -R y2_) testbed/y2/scripts/deploy-fw.sh, select-ui.sh deploy and UI selection

The layout follows the RP2350 target (platforms/<name>/ with its own main.c and hal/), not hal/host, because this target has its own toolchain and device HALs. The host build stays the place where HALs are simulated.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
scripts/build.sh y2                      # build/y2/platforms/y2/neupod (and neupod.stripped)

The compiler is the Buildroot cross toolchain that built the rootfs, so the C library matches the device exactly. By default ~/y2-build/out-rootfs/host/bin/arm-buildroot-linux-gnueabihf-gcc; point somewhere else with -DNEUPOD_Y2_TOOLCHAIN_DIR=<dir> and -DNEUPOD_Y2_TRIPLE=<triple> or the environment variables NEUPOD_Y2_TOOLCHAIN / NEUPOD_Y2_TRIPLE. The secrets code needs mbed TLS from the Pico SDK (PICO_SDK_PATH) as on the other targets.

CI cannot use the Buildroot toolchain, so the y2 job in .github/workflows/firmware.yml cross-builds with the Ubuntu gcc-arm-linux-gnueabihf package (about 20 s of installing) and checks that the result is a 32-bit ARM hard-float executable. That binary is a compile check; only the Buildroot-built one is deployed. The portable Y2 logic is also covered by the host job's ctest.

docs.title: What each HAL does
docs.text: HAL On the Y2 Display /dev/fb0 (mtkfb, 480x360, three pages, XRGB8888). The HAL keeps an RGB565 shadow frame with the ST7789-style window and cursor, so the UI draws as on every target, and hal_display_present() converts only the rows that changed into the next page and flips to it with pan plus put (about 64 fps for full frames measured on the device). Nothing is flipped when nothing was drawn. A previous run can leave the pan offset on another page, so the HAL pans to page 0 when it opens. hal_display_width()/height() report 480x360. Brightness is /sys/class/leds/lcd-backlight/brightness (0..255); sleep and wake switch the backlight off and on. Input The wheel and ring buttons are the mtk-tpd evdev node, the side keys mtk-kpd, found by name under /sys/class/input. A wheel detent is one KEY_DOWN (clockwise) or KEY_UP press; it moves a virtual finger by 4 wheel positions, the same as a console s or w, so each detent is one list step and the UI's scroll acceleration applies as on the real wheel. Centre (KEY_ENTER) keeps its real hold time, Menu is KEY_BACK, Prev/Next are KEY_LEFT/KEY_RIGHT, Play/Pause is KEY_PLAYPAUSE. A wheel tick within 150 ms after a Centre, Prev or Next press is dropped (a finger brushing the wheel on its way to the button); Menu and Play do not suppress the wheel, because the usual thing after Menu is to scroll the list that appears. A button pressed and released between two polls (the nodes are read every 8 ms) still gives its press and release, one poll apart. Vol+/Vol- call player_volume_step() (one step per press, repeating while held). Power key (since ADR-0020; the HAL only reports it as a level, hal_input_power_key(), and the UI decides what a press means, see UI): a tap (under 0.4 s) turns the screen off at once (backlight off; with Auto-lock on, Hold turns on) and the next input of any kind wakes it and is not delivered; held 2 s (it fires at 2 s while still held, once, not on release) it toggles Hold (lock / unlock, with a bar from 0.4 s, a confirmation, a haptic click and a lock glyph in the status bar); held on, a "Powering off in 5" countdown appears at 5 s (letting go cancels) and at 10 s it logs y2: power held, shutting down and runs the firmware's ordinary clean stop (the same path as SIGTERM: the storage task finishes, card writes are locked, the card is synced and unmounted), then starts /sbin/poweroff detached in its own session and exits with status 77, which tells the S91neupod-fw respawn wrapper not to restart it at once. The wrapper waits 15 s (NEUPOD_POWEROFF_WAIT overrides, for tests); init's stop scripts end it during that wait, and nothing waits on anything else, so there is no double stop. If the system is still up after 15 s the wrapper logs poweroff did not happen, restarting and respawns the firmware, so a failed poweroff never leaves a dead screen. If /sbin/poweroff cannot be started at all the firmware exits 0 and is respawned. (Before ADR-0020 the HAL itself slept the screen on a short press, swallowed input while asleep except Power and Centre/Menu, and powered off at 2 s. All of that moved to the UI; if the side-key node closes mid-press the held Power press is forgotten and reported as released.) The Y2 has no Hold slide switch (hal_input_hold_switch() says none). The command can be replaced with the environment variable NEUPOD_Y2_POWEROFF (absolute path, no arguments) or -DY2_POWEROFF_CMD=...; host tests use it so they never power off the PC. The nodes are drained every 8 ms. Console keys w s scroll, e select, m menu, a d left/right, p play. Read from stdin when it is a terminal or pipe, and from a control FIFO, /run/neupod.keys (NEUPOD_KEYS_FIFO overrides the path): ssh root@y2 'echo s > /run/neupod.keys'. On the FIFO and on piped stdin a newline is ignored, so echo s is one scroll step and not also Select. A stdin that is /dev/null or ends is dropped; the process keeps running. Storage The microSD as a raw block device under FatFs, the same layering as the Pico (see below). Charging-only mode When the Y2 is "off" with USB attached, stock LK boots the kernel again in power-off-charging mode: /proc/cmdline shows boot_reason=1 (BR_USB) and /sys/class/BOOT/BOOT/boot/boot_mode reads 8 (KERNEL_POWER_OFF_CHARGING) or 9 (LOW_POWER_OFF_CHARGING). main() reads that file first (before any HAL init) and logs y2: boot_mode N (charging|normal); an absent, empty or unreadable file counts as a normal boot. In mode 8 or 9 the firmware starts no UI, storage, audio or FreeRTOS and runs y2_charging_main() (platforms/y2/charging.c): framebuffer mapped once and cleared, then a 250 ms sleep loop (idles near 0 % CPU) reading the mtk-kpd (side keys) and mtk-tpd (wheel) nodes. Screen: for 10 s after entering the mode, and again after every key press or wheel touch, the backlight is on (brightness 255) and an own-artwork animated battery is drawn straight into the framebuffer (y2_chargeview.c, no LVGL: dark theme colours, 5 segments that fill one by one up to the current level, hold one step and start again every 600 ms; green, red at 15 % or less; the percentage and CHARGING below). The gauge saying Full or Not charging with the charger present shows a still full battery captioned CHARGED. No gauge reading shows an empty battery and --%. While Power is held an amber HOLD TO RESTART caption and a bar fill over the 2 s. After the 10 s the backlight goes to 0 and nothing is read or drawn until the next key. Only the backlight node and /dev/fb0 are written. The picture is size-independent (the panel is 480x360; the tests draw 320x240 as well, ctest -R y2_chargeview, snapshots in build/host/snapshots_charging). Power held 2 s (this mode has its own loop and timer, y2_charge; the 10 s player gesture does not apply): logs, spawns /sbin/reboot detached (override NEUPOD_Y2_REBOOT or -DY2_REBOOT_CMD=...) once per press and exits 77, so S91neupod-fw does not respawn at once (the 15 s "still up, restarting" fallback applies as in normal mode). Charger removed: every /sys/class/power_supply/* that is not the battery is read (online; every non-battery supply, on the device ac, usb and wireless; any one online counts; a missing or non-0/1 value counts as unreadable); after it has been continuously offline for 3 s (any online reading restarts the timer) it spawns /sbin/poweroff and exits 77. The 3 s timer is only armed once an online reading has been seen since the loop started (the charger can read 0 early in a charger boot); a charger that never reads online leaves the device up. If no charger supply can be read the state is "unknown" and never powers off. A short Power press only wakes the screen. SIGTERM exits 0 (the wrapper would respawn it, but init stop kills the whole group first). If a command cannot be started it is logged and retried (next hold, or after another 3 s offline). S90neupod-demo skips itself in boot mode 8 or 9 when /opt/neupod-fw/neupod is executable (on a demo-only device it behaves as before); command line arguments such as --run-ms are ignored in charging mode and logged as such. S91neupod-fw starts the firmware in that mode whatever /etc/neupod-ui says; both read the mode from NEUPOD_BOOT_MODE_FILE (default the sysfs path) so they can be tested in a sandbox. select-ui.sh demo run while the device is in charging-only mode will not start the demo (and will roll back). Not tried on the device yet: the picture, its timing and the backlight on/off have only been checked on the PC (rendering and timer tests, snapshots); the loop, the Power hold and the unplug path are unit-tested (y2_charge, y2_sysfs) and the init-script logic was run in a sandbox with fake sysfs and binaries; on the bench, reboot from this mode with USB attached came back with boot_mode=0 and boot_reason=4, a normal boot, so there is no charging loop (real power_supply nodes: ac, battery, usb, wireless; usb/online=1 when plugged). Battery /sys/class/power_supply/battery: capacity, batt_vol (mV; voltage_now in microvolts is also accepted) and status. There is no charge-rate reading, so while charging or discharging the rate is a fixed plus or minus 10 %/h, which is what makes the UI show "charging" or "discharging". Gauge-chip calls (alert threshold, hibernate, reset) answer "not supported". Audio Wired headphones: the CS43131 DAC behind the MT6582's audio unit, through /dev/cs43131_dac and /dev/eac (hal_audio.c; the logic, with its safety allow-lists and state machine, is y2_audio.c, host test y2_audio). Used only while /sys/class/switch/h2w reports headphones (state 1 or 2; the DAC driver does the detect), 44.1 kHz / 16 bit only (other rates are resampled or refused as for any fixed-rate sink), and the backend is cs43131 when both nodes open, which is what makes the boot check pass; otherwise it is a timed null sink and the check says audio is degraded. The same stream also drives the internal speaker and Line out (below). The audio core's 32-bit blocks go through a lock-free ring (4096 frames) to a plain pthread that does blocking write() on /dev/eac, so the DAC's own clock paces the player (the block clock waits for room in the ring instead of a timer); that thread never calls the RTOS. 32 to 16 bit is rounded with TPDF dither whenever bits below the 16th are set (any volume below 0 dB), bit-exact otherwise. Volume: the CS43131's hardware index is fixed at 11 (register 0x29, -20.5 dB, about 0.2 Vrms at full scale) and the user volume stays the software volume (2 dB steps, -30 dB at power-up); NEUPOD_Y2_DAC_INDEX=n in /etc/neupod-fw.env overrides it (0 to 11, clamped; unparseable = 11). Clicks: the DAC is powered (0x4302, stereo 0x4307) by the first audible block, not at boot, and stays on across tracks and pauses; its volume is set to mute (index 0, the kernel applies it 80 ms later) before the stream is torn down or the DAC powered down and restored after the stream is running, followed by 100 ms of silence before the audio. Digital silence for 3 s stops the AFE stream (DAC stays on); 30 s after that the DAC is powered down (0x4303); a clean stop does it too. Headphones pulled out: stream and DAC stopped at once (within the 200 ms jack poll), and while playing on the wired output the audio route pauses with the banner Headphones unplugged (plugging back in does not resume). Output routing: Auto uses Bluetooth while a headset stream is open (the DAC is left alone), else the jack when headphones are in, else the speaker when Settings > Speaker is On (see below). A device error falls back to the null sink for 5 s, then retries. Only whitelisted AFE offsets (0x10, 0x14, 0x20, 0x4c, 0x3a0, 0x3ac, 0x4c4) and device commands are ever issued: never the PMIC registers, the speaker amplifier ioctls other than SET_SPEAKER_ON / OFF (0x400443a1 / a2), the CS43131 init or debug register file; 0x4306 (mono) only in a speaker session. Log lines: audio: DAC on, stream started, stream stopped after 3 s of silence, DAC powered down, and every 10 s while streaming underruns=... write_us avg/max=.... Radio Bluetooth only (docs/bluetooth.md): BTstack over the combo chip's /dev/stpbt on a thread of its own, started by hal_bt_init(). hal_system_late_init() reports the radio present only if /data/BT_Addr is a valid address and /dev/stpbt opens (the init script S80mtk-bt makes that so; without /opt/mtk-wmt staged it does nothing and Bluetooth is greyed out). Wi-Fi is not present: the boot check marks it unavailable and the hal_wifi_* calls answer "no device". Haptics The ERM motor behind /sys/class/timed_output/vibrator/enable (writing N switches it on for N ms), through platforms/y2/hal/hal_haptic.c, which implements hal_haptic.h in place of the DRV2605L driver (no I2C is faked; hal_i2c stays a stub). The boot check opens the node for writing and logs haptics: timed_output vibrator (ERM); if it is missing or not writable the check reports haptics unavailable as timed_output vibrator: no response (and the full reason on the console). The app's click (one per wheel detent, the ERM click effect 3) is a tick. Calls come from the app's haptic task, never from the input or UI path (the UI only drops a byte in a non-blocking queue), and each pulse is one short write opened with O_CLOEXEC. A rest of 45 ms after each pulse (on top of the task's 35 ms request gap) coalesces a fast scroll into separate taps, not a continuous buzz. Pulse lengths, one table: tick 15 ms, click 30 ms, strong 60 ms (DRV2605 ROM ids 3, 6, 9, 12, 24-26 are ticks; 1, 4, 10, 14 strong; the rest clicks).
