Entries are positions in the range; the path the queue hands the storage task is a handle, @lib/<order>/<position>, which the storage task turns into the file when the track starts or the gapless look-ahead asks for it (lib_resolve: order file, track record, folder chain and names: four small files, one open at a time, an estimated 20 ms on the card; it is asked while the current track plays, so the audio ring is not at risk). Shuffle is the stateless keyed permutation of the ADR (a balanced 4-round Feistel network over the next even power of two, cycle-walked), so Shuffle Songs over the whole library keeps no array, visits every song once, keeps the current song current when shuffle is switched on or off, and re-keys for each round of repeat-all (never opening with the song just played). A gapless successor that the audio core took but the plan no longer names re-bases the permutation on that song. queue_len / queue_pos and the queue's entries are 32 bit now. Shuffle Songs forces a shuffled queue without changing the Shuffle setting; the folder queue and its 128-track window are as before.
  • Unplayable files (D6). Greyed in every list; Select says why instead of opening it. The queue does not skip them itself: the storage task refuses an unplayable handle with Can't play: ..., and the player's existing rule (a track the queue moved on to that cannot be played is skipped; a whole lap of them under repeat-all ends in the error) does the rest, so Next, auto-advance and Shuffle step past them with the same bounded loop.
  • Resume. The record is written from the real path (the storage task keeps the last two resolved handles' paths for the player, player_set_path_resolver), so a library track resumes as a folder queue of its own folder, at its frame. The queue itself (the album or the shuffle) is not restored; a track that has not been resolved when its record would be written waits for the next save. Library queues keep no shuffle seed across a boot.
  • Building. The first open of a top-level list without an index (and Shuffle Songs) starts the build itself, Music > Update Library rebuilds on demand (decision: an explicit action in Music rather than Settings; Settings is where the Bluetooth branch changes). Progress is the file count (n songs found) with busy dots, not a percentage: the walk and the parse are one pass, so the total is not known until it ends; the sort and the write after it have no per-file callback and no cancel point. Cancel and "another request is waiting" (a Play press, a folder listing) stop the scan at its next file; the old library is untouched and lib.tmp is removed. Nothing is written before Library needs a writable card is ruled out: a write-protected card is answered up front, and a write the card refuses later (the Y2's reopen read-write failing) is reported the same way.
  • Not built: playlists (the entry says None yet), letter jumps (the fast-scroll letter overlay is shown; the jump tables are in the manifest), the fingerprint check at boot and incremental rescans (L3), Right on an artist jumping to its albums (Right / Left skip tracks, as on every other screen).
  • Host. The simulator's card is a folder, not a FatFs volume, so its build of the library uses lib_ff_posix.h, the dozen FatFs-style calls the library makes, over POSIX files (hal/host/lib_ff_posix.c, paths kept inside the card folder); the unit tests run the real FatFs on a disk image and the Y2 and RP2350 builds use theirs. The tour card is made by tests/tools/make_library_card.py: real FLAC test vectors with their tags replaced, an MP3, an AAC track, three silent 3 s WAVs; NEUPOD_LIB_SLOW_MS (simulator only) slows the scan so the progress screen can be photographed.

  • Measured. Host, POSIX files with a warm cache (the tour card plus real FLAC test vectors): 276 tracks in 131 ms and 1,016 tracks in 322 ms for the whole build (11 sort runs, 99 KB of scratch); L1's 100,000-file run on the FatFs image is unchanged by L2 (12 s). The device is not measured yet: the ADR's own figures (10-20 ms per parsed file) put about 260 FLACs at roughly 5 to 8 seconds, see Storage.

  • Index format 3 (12 November 2026, UI review LB-2b). The sort key also skips a leading "A " and "An " (as it already skipped "The "), so "A Perfect Circle" is under P. The order changes, so LIB_VERSION is 3: an index from a firmware before this fails the version check ("Library needs rebuilding") and the Music lists rebuild it by themselves on the next open, exactly as for format 2.

docs.title: ADR-0018: UI resolution profiles
docs.text: Status: accepted (owner decision 11 Nov 2026)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The UI was written for the Phase 1 panel, 320x240: UI_W / UI_H / UI_ROW_H constants plus pixel literals in every screen, Montserrat 14 / 20 / 48, two 320 x 24 render buffers. The Y2 Linux testbed (testbed/y2) has a 480x360 panel and runs the same firmware as a hosted build. Two ways to get the UI there: render at 320x240 and scale the frame up (blurry text, wasted pixels, a scaler in the display path), or render natively at 480x360.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• The UI is resolution-independent through a metrics profile. ui_metrics_t (app/ui/ui_metrics.h) holds every pixel size and the fonts; ui_task selects the profile once from hal_display_width() / hal_display_height() (the largest compiled-in profile that fits; 320x240 otherwise). Screens read UIM->...; nothing else scales a length.
  • 320x240 is the product panel and its profile holds the exact numbers the UI had before: the host snapshots at that size are unchanged (compared byte for byte against the previous build, apart from the build hash text and timing animation).
  • 480x360 is for the Y2 testbed (and for testing the hires layout on the host): every length x 3/2, fonts one step up (Montserrat 14 to 20, 20 to 28, 48 stays; it is the largest size built; the fonts are the project's own Latin-1 builds, see UI), 9 rows per page in both.
  • Hires fonts and buffers are compiled only for hosted builds. CMake option NEUPOD_UI_HIRES (default ON for host and y2, OFF for rp2350 and esp32s3) gates the 480x360 profile, Montserrat 28 (lv_conf.h), the 480 x 36 render buffers, a 192 KB LVGL pool and the layout audit. The product build keeps its 72 KB pool and its 2 x 15 KB render buffers.
  • Native over scaling. The owner chose native rendering on 11 Nov 2026.
  • The host HAL display size is selectable at run time (NEUPOD_DISPLAY_SIZE=WxH, default 320x240), so the hires layout runs in the simulator and in CI. That, hal_display.h wording and nothing else changed under hal/.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• RAM budget: RP2350 unchanged. The render buffers, LVGL pool, list row pool (UI_ROWS_MAX = 9) and every other static allocation of the product build keep their sizes. Hosted builds: render buffers 2 x 34 KB, pool 192 KB (measured peak 69 KB across every tour at 480x360).
  • Flash budget (RP2350): the product build has one profile, defined as a header constant, so every field read folds into an immediate and the metrics cost nothing; measured on 11 Nov 2026 (Release, neupod.elf): text 1,289,412 B before and after (0 B), .data 0 and .bss 489,348 B unchanged (the display, i2c and storage test images are byte-for-byte the same size). Montserrat 28 is now compiled out of the product build; it was enabled but unreferenced, so the linker had already dropped it (no size effect, it just keeps the guarantee explicit). An earlier version with a run-time pointer to the table grew the image by 2.8 KB, which is why the product build does not select a profile at run time.
  • Layout is checked, not eyeballed: tests/test_ui_metrics.c (static invariants of every profile), the tours at 480x360 with the layout audit (ui_audit.c, NEUPOD_UI_AUDIT=1) and hires_art_snapshot (pixel checks of the art boxes).
  • Known limits at 480x360: album art is still decoded to 64 x 64 (ART_MAX_DIM; raising it costs 8 KB per step of static RAM on the product build and changes the art snapshots) and scaled up 2.6x by LVGL; the splash wordmark stays at 48 pt; the bring-up scenes (gfx_strip, display tests) are 320x240 only.
  • Another panel size needs one profile (one initialiser in ui_metrics.c) and, if it is larger than 480x360, bigger UI_BUF_W_MAX / UI_BUF_LINES_MAX and the host HAL's 640x480 ceiling raised.
  • The input path is untouched: wheel, keys and the Y2 buttons all deliver the same events.

docs.title: ADR-0019: Bluetooth audio output behind a stack-neutral boundary
Status
docs.text: Accepted (owner decisions, 12 Nov 2026): keep BTstack, and build the audio sink so the stack can be swapped cheaply. The owner's answers to the design questions are recorded at the end.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• Stage 2a (Bluetooth) built pairing and the connection on the RP2350 + CYW43439 with BTstack. It is behind hal_bt_* in hal/include/hal_radio.h, and the BTstack code sits in one file, platforms/rp2350/hal/hal_radio_bt.c. That file mixes three things: BTstack's link logic (pairing state machine, SDP, TLV glue), the CYW43 transport and its run loop, and the Pico SDK hooks.
  • There is no audio yet. hal_radio_a2dp_connect() / _disconnect() are declared but not implemented.
  • On 12 Nov 2026 the Y2 testbed streamed A2DP to AirPods Pro and a Sony WI-C200. It used BTstack over the MT6582's /dev/stpbt (testbed/y2/tools/y2-a2dp, a standalone tool) and played a tone and a FLAC from the card. Two platforms now have a working BTstack controller, each with a different transport and run loop.
  • Licence. BTstack is free for non-commercial use only (Bluetooth → Licence). The owner does not expect neuPod ever to be sold (12 Nov 2026), so BTstack is acceptable. It still has to stay replaceable: a licensed BTstack, Zephyr's host or ESP-IDF Bluedroid (ADR-0007 update) are the alternatives.

docs.title: 1. One boundary: hal_bt_*, extended for audio
docs.text:
Everything above the HAL (app/runtime/bt_service.c, the player, the audio engine, the UI) sees hal_radio.h only. No BTstack type, header or constant crosses it. That rule already holds; the decision is to keep it for audio. Stage 2b adds, replacing the hal_radio_a2dp_* stubs:

Addition Purpose hal_bt_stream_open() / _start() / _suspend() / _close() A2DP stream on the CONNECTED link. Asynchronous; progress through events. hal_bt_codec_t (codec, rate, channels, mode, bitpool_min/max, kbps) The negotiated configuration, for the badge and the stats. The enum names SBC, SBC-XQ (and AAC / aptX for a stack or module that has them). HAL_BT_EVT_STREAM (OPENING, OPEN, STREAMING, SUSPENDED, CLOSED, FAILED + reason) Stream state. HAL_BT_EVT_VOLUME (0..127, absolute) AVRCP absolute volume from the headset. hal_bt_volume_set(0..127) Our volume to the headset. HAL_BT_EVT_KEY (PLAY, PAUSE, PLAY_PAUSE, NEXT, PREV, STOP) AVRCP passthrough from the headset buttons. hal_bt_track_info() Title, artist, album, duration and position for AVRCP metadata (2c). hal_bt_stats_t Encoded frames, packets sent, ring underruns, drift corrections, link quality where the controller reports it.

PCM does not go through hal_bt_*. It goes through the core 1 to core 0 ring of ADR-0013 (4 Nov amendment). The encoder side drains the ring. The audio engine treats Bluetooth as one more output: it selects "Bluetooth", fills the ring, and never knows which stack encodes it.

docs.title: 2. BTstack in one adapter, transports per platform
docs.text:
The BTstack code is split into:

  • hal/common/bt_btstack/ (platform-neutral, built by every platform that uses BTstack): the link state machine moved out of hal_radio_bt.c, the A2DP source, the AVRCP target and controller, the SBC encoder feed and pacing (the source-side pacing model in Bluetooth), the TLV bridge onto hal_bt_storage_t, and the implementation of every hal_bt_* function.
  • Per-platform glue (bt_port.h: init the transport, give the run loop, post to it, local address, power):
  • platforms/rp2350/hal/bt_port_cyw43.c: the CYW43 transport and async_context run loop, as now.
  • platforms/y2/hal/bt_port_stpbt.c: btstack_uart_stpbt + btstack_chipset_mtk_consys (promoted from the testbed tool) and the POSIX run loop on its own pthread.

Swapping the stack means writing a new hal/common/bt_<stack>/ against the same hal_radio.h and the same bt_port.h. Nothing above the HAL changes, and nor do its tests.

docs.title: 3. The host simulator implements the whole API
docs.text: hal/host/hal_radio.c grows the stream, codec, volume and key events (and a simulated drop) so every UI and player behaviour below runs in host tests and tours without a radio. The simulator and the BTstack adapter are two implementations of one contract. A contract test (tests/test_hal_bt_contract.c) drives both where it can: the simulator in CI, BTstack against a fake controller (as test_hci_preinit does in the y2-a2dp tool).

docs.title: 4. The Y2 becomes a Bluetooth platform
docs.text: The firmware on the Y2 gets real Bluetooth through bt_port_stpbt.c, instead of the "not present" stubs in platforms/y2/hal/hal_radio.c. The WMT bring-up (stock wmt_loader once per boot, 6620_launcher, the property area, the device nodes) moves into the Y2 init scripts ahead of the firmware, and hal_bt_init() opens /dev/stpbt. The testbed rules hold: MTK blobs are staged from the backup, never committed; NVRAM is never written. y2-a2dp stays as the bench tool.

docs.title: 5. The UI is part of stage 2b, not an afterthought
docs.text:
Every state that the boundary can report has a screen, and every one is in a host tour with a snapshot:

Where What Status bar Bluetooth icon: grey = remembered headset not connected, white = connected, accent colour = streaming. Hidden when Bluetooth is unavailable. Now Playing The format badge shows the negotiated codec on Bluetooth output (SBC 44.1, SBC-XQ); the source format stays in the stats. On Bluetooth the volume bar is the headset volume. Volume With absolute volume the wheel sends hal_bt_volume_set() and the software volume stays at 0 dB; the headset's own volume changes move the bar. Without it, the wheel is the software volume, as on I2S. One mapping table, host-tested. Headset buttons HAL_BT_EVT_KEY becomes the same player actions as Play / Right / Left, on every screen. Link lost while playing The player pauses at once (ring emptied, position kept). A banner reads Headset disconnected for 3 s. The output stays Bluetooth: nothing plays from the wired output by itself. Settings > Bluetooth Paired, no audio yet is gone. The headset row shows Connected - SBC-XQ / Streaming / Not connected / Failed: <reason>. A new Audio output: Auto / Wired row (Auto = Bluetooth whenever a headset is connected; saved on the card). The right-hand pane adds codec, bitpool, kbit/s, underruns. Devices Unchanged apart from the wording above. Pairing a second headset while one is remembered asks to replace it (one headset, as now). Settings > About Bluetooth stats line (frames, underruns, drift corrections). Errors Every new hal_bt_fail_t reason gets its phrase in hal_bt_fail_text() (19 characters max) and a tour snapshot.

Tours: --tour-bt is extended with bt-streaming, np-bt-badge, np-bt-volume, bt-dropped and bt-key-next, at 320x240 and 480x360 (ADR-0018).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• hal_radio_bt.c is split before the A2DP work starts. That is a no-behaviour-change refactor of stage 2a, proven by the existing 2a tests and the bench Pair / reconnect / Forget on the WI-C200 (RP2350) before anything new is added.
  • The Y2 can prove the A2DP source, pacing, AVRCP and the whole UI on real headsets while the RP2350 path is still RAM-constrained. Bugs found there are in shared code, so the fix lands on both.
  • A different stack later costs one adapter and its glue. A QCC/BM83 module would be an adapter that speaks the module's UART protocol instead of HCI, behind the same API.
  • The core 1 rules (ADR-0011) are unchanged: core 1 only fills the ring; all Bluetooth work is on core 0. The closure check covers the ring.
  • RAM budget: the boundary itself costs nothing (header types, one event struct grows by about 24 B). RP2350: SBC encoder state and media buffers are measured in 2b and come out of free SRAM (about 14.9 KB). The PCM ring reuses the I2S ring storage (ADR-0013 amendment). Y2: not constrained. Flash, RP2350: A2DP + AVRCP + SBC encoder, measured in 2b.

docs.title: Owner decisions (12 Nov 2026)
docs.text:
1. Split now. The BTstack link logic moves out of platforms/rp2350/hal/hal_radio_bt.c into hal/common/bt_btstack/ before 2b, as a no-behaviour-change refactor.
  2. Link lost while playing: pause and stay on Bluetooth (position kept, banner); no fallback to wired output.
  3. Output selection: automatic, with an Audio output: Auto / Wired row to force wired.
  4. Volume: AVRCP absolute volume to the headset with the software volume at 0 dB; software volume when the headset has no absolute volume.
  5. Y2 as a Bluetooth platform: yes, the real stack goes into the Y2 firmware (taken as the default; not asked separately).

docs.title: Amendment 12 Nov 2026: stage 2b as built
docs.text:
Details and the RAM / flash figures are in Bluetooth. Differences from the decision above, all deliberate:

  • hal_bt_set_pcm_source() hands the stack the consumer side of the PCM ring (a small type in hal/include/hal_bt_pcm.h). PCM still does not travel through hal_bt_*; the stack pulls it from the ring on its own thread.
  • 44.1 kHz only. One SBC endpoint at 44.1 kHz; tracks at other rates are refused on the Bluetooth output. 48 kHz and the hi-res decimation of ADR-0013 are a follow-up.
  • Declared in 2c (see below): HAL_BT_EVT_VOLUME, hal_bt_volume_set, HAL_BT_EVT_KEY, hal_bt_track_info; the Now Playing volume bar and the headset buttons.
  • Two new failure reasons, HAL_BT_FAIL_STREAM ("audio refused") and HAL_BT_FAIL_CODEC ("no common format"); the status-bar glyph uses the text colour for "connected" because the bar is light.

docs.title: Amendment 12 Nov 2026: stage 2c as built, and reconnect
docs.text:
Details in Bluetooth. Differences from the decision above:

  • The volume path is the AVRCP controller role (the headset is the target of absolute volume); the AVRCP target carries the buttons and the metadata. hal_bt_volume_supported() / hal_bt_volume_get() are added to the boundary, HAL_BT_EVT_KEY also has FF and RW, and hal_bt_track_info() returns false when the stack is busy.
  • Volume cap on connect (owner decision, 12 Nov 2026): a headset whose first absolute-volume report on a connection is above 50 % (NEUPOD_BT_VOLUME_CAP_ON_CONNECT, 64 of 127) is turned down to 50 %, never up; later changes are the user's. Taking over the headset's volume releases the software attenuation, so a headset a phone left at 100 % would otherwise play full scale.
  • A headset-initiated AVDTP START (a stem click on a suspended stream) is delivered as HAL_BT_KEY_PLAY; every AVRCP pass-through and every remote START / SUSPEND is logged.
  • STOP from the headset pauses (the place is kept). No volume is remembered per headset.
  • Stage 3 reconnect is built early on the owner's request: after a lost link and at power-up, with backoff, ended by any user action; playback is not resumed.

docs.title: ADR-0020: Hold, the lock that replaces the iPod's slide switch
docs.text: Status: accepted (owner decisions 12 Nov 2026)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
A pocket player gets pressed by its own pocket. The iPod answered that with a slide switch ("Hold") that made the wheel and buttons do nothing. neuPod has to answer it on every platform it runs on:

  • the Y2 testbed has a Power key on its side and no slide switch;
  • the Pico 2 W bench rig has neither (UART console keys only);
  • the final board is the iPod 6G donor, which has the real slide switch.

Until now the Y2 had its own, partial answer inside the HAL: a short Power press put the screen to sleep (input swallowed except Power and Centre/Menu), a 2 s hold shut the player down. The screen dimmed after an idle time (UI-5, first half) but never went fully off.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
One Hold state, set from several places, enforced in one place (the UI frame).

  • Where it is enforced. ui_frame_input() (app/ui/ui_frame.c). While Hold is on, wheel turns and button presses and releases are swallowed before any screen sees them: they cannot act (Play/Pause included), cannot click, and cannot move anything. They only restart the idle clock (the screen wakes) and show a reminder ("Locked, hold Power to unlock"). Headset (AVRCP) keys do not go through the UI and keep working: they are deliberate. The Y2's side volume keys are hardware keys like the rest and are locked too (ui_locked(), checked where the Y2 handles them). Hold is RAM only: it is not saved over a power-off (a boot starts unlocked unless the switch says otherwise).
  • Auto-lock. When the screen goes off (below), Hold turns on by itself. Settings > Display > Auto-lock (On by default, saved) turns that off; Hold is then only set by hand.
  • Screen off (UI-5, second stage). After the dim (Settings > Display > Auto-dim / Dim after, unchanged) the backlight goes fully off after Screen off after (default 3 min after the dim; Never, 15 s, 30 s, 1, 2, 3, 5 min; counted from the last input when Auto-dim is off; saved). The input that wakes a screen that was off is not delivered to the screen, locked or not. A short Power press (released within 0.4 s) also turns the screen off at once, and the next input wakes it. The panel is not put to sleep: only the backlight goes (hal_display_backlight(0)), as before on the Y2.
  • The Power key. Reported by the HAL as a level (hal_input_power_key()), turned into INPUT_POWER_DOWN / _UP events by the input task (which never loses an edge: a lost release would count as a 10 s hold), timed by the UI (app/ui/ui_hold.c, unit tested):
Held What happens under 0.4 s (a tap) screen off now (and Hold on, with Auto-lock) 0.4 s to 2 s a line under the status bar fills and a pill says "Keep holding to lock" / "... to unlock"; releasing early does nothing 2 s, still held Hold toggles: a confirmation ("Locked" / "Unlocked"), a haptic click where fitted, the lock icon in the status bar 5 s still held: "Release to cancel · shutting down in 5" with a red line that grows; releasing cancels 10 s power-off is requested (hal_system_poweroff())

The power-off countdown only exists where hal_system_can_poweroff() is true (the Y2; the host simulator pretends). The Y2 keeps its contract: the request runs the firmware's orderly stop, starts /sbin/poweroff detached and exits with status 77 so S91neupod-fw does not respawn it. What changed is the timing (10 s, was 2 s) and who decides (the UI, not the HAL). Charging-only mode is untouched: its own loop still reboots on a 2 s hold (y2_charge). * The hardware switch. hal_input_hold_switch() reports NONE / OFF / ON. A change becomes INPUT_HOLD_SWITCH and sets the same Hold state (on = locked, off = unlocked); a switch found on at boot locks at once. The Power gesture still toggles too, so the two agree after any change. Platforms without a switch report NONE: the Y2 and the Pico rig. The final board's GPIO is a TODO(hw). * No Power key (Pico 2 W bench): Hold is gesture-only there. The console key l toggles Hold (INPUT_HOLD_TOGGLE), and the reminder says "Console key l unlocks" instead of "hold Power 2 s to unlock". The bench rig cannot power itself off, so no countdown. * Host simulator: F1 is the Power key (hold it), and tour tokens pwr:down, pwr:up, sleep:MS and sw:on / sw:off drive the Power key and the switch from scripts.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• RAM budget: about 100 B of statics (Hold state, the pump state, the overlay's object pointers); the overlay's four LVGL objects exist only while something is shown (a few hundred bytes of the LVGL pool, freed after). The input queue grows from 16 to 64 events (+384 B, see UI-6 in Runtime). Measured sizes are in the pull request.
  • Flash: three glyphs (lock, unlock, power) in the three UI fonts, the Hold logic and the Licences data (see the pull request for the figures).
  • Y2 behaviour change: the HAL no longer sleeps the screen or swallows input by itself, and a 2 s hold no longer powers off (it toggles Hold; 10 s powers off). docs/y2.md describes the new behaviour.
  • A press that wakes the screen is lost on purpose, locked or not: that is the price of a pocket-proof player.
  • A button held down when Hold comes on (a fast-forward in progress) still gets its release: the frame remembers which presses a screen saw and delivers exactly those releases while locked, so nothing is left pressed.
  • Tests: ui_hold (the timing model), ui_frame_keys (what the frame swallows and when), ui_logic (the off stage), input_events (the hand-over and the console key), y2_input, and the hold_tour / hires_hold_tour runs (ring, lock, swallowed keys, countdown, simulated power-off, switch, screen off, wake, unlock, the new Display rows) with the layout audit at 320x240 and 480x360.

docs.title: Amendment 12 November 2026: the visuals are the lock pill and the Power-hold line
docs.text: The overlay box of this ADR (a boxed headline, a second line and a progress bar over the middle of the content) is replaced by the design review's HL-1 (UI design review, section 3.8): a dark pill at the bottom of the screen with one line of text, and a 3 px line under the status bar (accent while a Power press fills towards the toggle, red for the power-off countdown). Nothing behind them is dimmed or blended, so only the pill and the line are repainted. The gestures, timings, the swallowed input, the switch and the power-off contract are unchanged. The texts: "Keep holding to lock · 10 s = off" (no "10 s = off" where the platform cannot power off), "Locked" / "Unlocked", "Locked · hold Power 2 s to unlock" for a swallowed key, "Release to cancel · shutting down in N", "Powering off". The lock icon is a Lucide icon in the status bar's right-hand group. RAM: the pill, its label and the line are built once with the frame (a few hundred bytes of the LVGL pool) instead of being built and deleted per use.

docs.title: UI design review, 12 November 2026
docs.text:
An owner-commissioned design review of the firmware UI (164 simulator screenshots reviewed). This folder holds the review as delivered:

  • REPORT.md: findings, the design system (colour tokens, type scale, layout metrics, icons, motion), a proposal per screen and the backlog (DS-*, NP-*, LB-*, BT-*, ST-*, IN-*, HL-*, FL-*, SP-*).
  • mockups/: every proposed screen at 320x240 and 480x360 (<area>-<screen>-<WxH>.png).
  • render.py: regenerates the mock-ups; every length comes from the metric table, so it doubles as a layout reference.

The backlog is tracked in Backlog; the implemented design system is described in UI mock-ups.

The mock-ups are drawn with Inter as a stand-in. Implementations use Montserrat Medium (the fonts the firmware already builds), which runs about 4 % wider; the review left that margin.

docs.title: Owner decisions (12 November 2026)
docs.text:
Where the review conflicts with earlier decisions, these win, in every phase:

  1. Now Playing. Select opens page 2; hold Select enters seek (the wheel seeks, Select commits, Menu cancels). This supersedes the earlier "Select toggles volume / seek". Built in phase 2.
  2. Bluetooth link lost. ADR-0019 stands: playback pauses and stays on Bluetooth; the firmware never switches the output by itself. The review's "Couldn't reconnect, playing on wired" toast becomes "Couldn't reconnect — paused".
  3. Theme. Light by default. Settings > Display > Theme is Light / Dark / Auto; Auto means dark once the backlight dims.
  4. Order. Phase 1 foundation (DS-*, HL-1), phase 2 Now Playing and library rows / fast scroll, phase 3 Bluetooth screens, phase 4 the rest.
  5. Platform. The Pico 2 W is frozen (ADR-0001 amendment). Design for the RP2350B with PSRAM and the Y2; ignore the review's "Pico 2 W" fallbacks, but keep that build compiling.
  6. Licences. Standing rule: every third-party asset added (Lucide icons, ISC; new font sizes, OFL) goes into LICENSE.md and the on-device Licences screen (app/ui/ui_licence_data.c); the licences ctest checks they agree.
  7. Dark accent. The dark theme's accent is #2868D8 (RGB565-safe, about 5:1 with white text); the review's #3078E8 gave 4.2:1. The contrast test asserts at least 4.5 in both themes.
  8. Toast height. The toast strip covers exactly one list row (30 px at 320x240, 45 px at 480x360), not 22 / 33 px.
  9. Auto theme stays as built. Auto is dark while the backlight is dimmed or off and light otherwise. With Auto-dim turned off the backlight never dims, so Auto behaves like Light (until the screen goes off).
  10. Text that does not fit scrolls (supersedes the review's "always an ellipsis"). One-line text wider than its box runs as a ticker: it waits 1 s, then scrolls round at about 35 px/s (52 px/s on 480x360) with a small gap between repeats, and only while it overflows. Where it applies: the Home track title and artist, the focused list row's main text (unfocused rows keep the ellipsis, like classic wheel players), the status-bar title; and, as a standing rule, Now Playing title / artist / album in phase 2 and any later one-line text. It stops and rewinds when focus leaves the row, and stands still while the screen is off. Tours snapshot every ticker at its start position.

docs.title: neuPod UI/UX review and proposal
docs.text:
Reviewed: 164 simulator screenshots (320x240/, 480x360/, two contact sheets), firmware v0.1.0-dev. Target: LVGL 9, RGB565, partial redraws, Montserrat Medium 14/20/48 (320×240) and 20/28/48 (480×360), click wheel + Select + 4 buttons + Hold.

Mock-ups are in mockups/, named <area>-<screen>-<WxH>.png, rendered at native resolution for both profiles. They use Inter Medium/SemiBold as a stand-in for Montserrat Medium (same x-height class; expect Montserrat to run ~4% wider — all widths below leave that margin). Fixture names (Aurora Lane, Harbour Lights, Beacon) are kept so the engineer can compare like for like.

docs.title: 1. Summary — highest-impact changes, ranked
docs.text:
1. Now Playing hierarchy — title/artist/album stack, format and output as pills, progress with remaining time, volume as a quiet bottom strip; one layout for wired and Bluetooth (np-nowplaying, np-nowplaying-bt). Today the title is a file name, "Playing – 1 of 3" competes with the format, and the volume bar is as heavy as the progress bar.
  2. Two-line list rows with secondary text for Songs and search results (lib-songs) — today artist is right-aligned on the same line and collides with long titles (lib-songs.png, text-nowplaying.png).
  3. Fast-scroll letter overlay + index rail (lib-songs-fastscroll) — the wheel accelerates but gives no position feedback; the overlay already exists in Files (files-many.png, the "F" tile) and should be generalised and moved off the content.
  4. Consistent status bar: left context slot (clock / track position / count / path), centre title, right Bluetooth + battery with a percentage when < 20 % (home-home). Today the left slot is always empty and the battery reads "--".
  5. Selection bar as the one accent: 4 px radius, 3 px inset from the edges, only the focused row coloured; chevrons and secondary text drop to grey — the bar then "moves" between rows with an 80 ms slide instead of repainting two rows.
  6. State feedback without modal screens: top toast strip for link-lost / can't-play / library busy (bt-dropped), bottom HUD strip for volume from any screen (np-volume-hud), and busy dots replaced by a determinate progress bar where a count is known (lib-building).
  7. Hold / Power feedback (hold-locked, hold-power-progress) — a pill at the bottom and a 3 px progress line under the status bar; no full-screen dim.
  8. Text entry on the wheel (in-text) — a horizontal letter ring with the current glyph at 48 px, mode chips (abc / ABC / 123 / #!? / space / ⌫) on Left/Right, field at the top. Today letters are evenly spaced small glyphs and there is no visible mode switch (in-text.png, wifi-kb.png).
  9. Dark theme via tokens (home-home-dark, np-nowplaying-dark) — one token table, Auto switches to dark when the backlight dims; the product board's LCD benefits less than an OLED would, but night use and battery on a future panel both improve.
  10. Missing screens: Cover-Flow-style album browser without 3D (lib-coverflow), Now Playing page 2 (np-page2), Playlists (lib-playlists), Licences (settings-licences), real empty states (lib-empty).

docs.title: 2.1 Colour tokens (RGB565-safe: R and B multiples of 8, G multiples of 4)
docs.text:
Token Light Dark Use bg #F8F8F8 #101010 screen background surface #FFFFFF #181818 cards, input fields, right pane bar #E8E8E8 #202020 status bar fill line #E0E0E0 #303030 hairlines, progress track, scrollbar track ink #181818 #F0F0F0 primary text, battery fill ink2 #606060 #A0A0A0 secondary text, chevrons, volume fill ink3 #A0A0A0 #686868 tertiary text, disabled rows, hints accent #1858C8 #2868D8 selection bar, progress fill, focused value on_accent #FFFFFF #FFFFFF text on the selection bar accent_soft #D8E4F8 #203050 pills, info toast amber #D08018 #E89828 seek mode, warnings amber_soft #F8E8C8 #483818 warning toast background green #209858 #30B870 charging, streaming OK, signal full red #D03028 #E84840 battery < 15 %, errors

Contrast: ink2 on surface 5.9:1 light / 7.1:1 dark; ink3 on surface 2.6:1 — use ink3 only for text ≥ 14 px that is not the sole carrier of meaning (hints, disabled rows). on_accent on accent 7.3:1.

Theme switch: a theme_t struct of these 14 colours; every style reads from it; lv_obj_report_style_change() after swap. Auto = light while the backlight is at full, dark once it dims (and remembers the user's last manual choice).

docs.title: 2.2 Type scale (existing fonts only)
docs.text:
Role 320×240 480×360 Weight Where Title 20 28 Medium Now Playing title, album header, empty-state heading Body 14 20 Medium list rows, status-bar title, settings values Small 12 (new) 16 (new) Medium secondary list line, times, pills, hints, status-bar left slot Big 48 48 Medium seek time, letter overlay, clock, text-entry current glyph

The only addition is Small (12 / 16 px). It is the single biggest readability gain in the proposal (secondary lines, times). Cost: one Montserrat Medium size per profile, ASCII + Latin-1 + punctuation ≈ 9–12 KB each. If flash is tight, ship 12 px only and let 480×360 use 14 px Body for secondary text with ink2 (works, looser).

Truncation: always LV_LABEL_LONG_DOT with a single ellipsis; never clip glyphs (text-nowplaying.png currently clips "Have You Fed t…" at the title size but wraps nothing). Title in Now Playing may wrap to two lines on 480×360 only.

docs.title: 2.3 Layout metrics
docs.text:
Metric 320×240 480×360 Status bar height 24 36 Single-line row 30 45 Two-line row 40 60 Horizontal padding 10 15 Selection bar inset / radius 3 / 4 4 / 6 Split-pane divider (Home, Settings) 56 % / 44 % same Art: Now Playing 112 168 Art: Home panel panel width − 24 same Art: album header, NP page 2 64 96 Art: Cover Flow centre / neighbours / outer 96 / 64 / 48 144 / 96 / 72 Progress bar height (normal / seek) 4 / 6 6 / 9 Toast strip height 22 33 HUD strip height 26 39 Pill height 18 27 Scrollbar width / margin 2 / 1 3 / 2

Visible rows: 320×240 gives 7 single-line rows or 5 two-line rows; 480×360 gives the same counts (everything scales ×1.5). Keep row counts identical across profiles so wheel acceleration feels the same.

docs.title: 2.4 Album-art sizes to decode
docs.text: Decode once per album to a 160×160 RGB565 thumbnail (51 KB) on the PSRAM board and keep an LRU of ~24 (1.2 MB). Draw it scaled down for every slot above; nothing is scaled up, which is what makes today's 64 px → 2.6× art look soft (art-cover.png). On the Pico 2 W target keep 96×96 (18 KB) and an LRU of 6; Now Playing then shows art at 1:1 on 320×240 and 1.17× on 480×360 — acceptable.

docs.title: 2.5 Icon set
docs.text:
Use Lucide (ISC licence, https://lucide.dev) rendered to 1-bit-alpha bitmaps at 16 and 24 px (320) / 24 and 36 px (480). Lucide is stroke-based, consistent at small sizes, and its licence permits embedding without attribution in the UI (keep the licence text in the Licences screen). Required glyphs, 14 in total:

chevron-right, play, pause, skip-back, skip-forward, shuffle, repeat, repeat-1, volume-2, bluetooth, wifi, lock, folder, file. Battery, signal bars and the three busy dots are drawn primitives (rectangles), not glyphs.

Drop FontAwesome where these cover it; keep it only for glyphs you already ship and still need.

docs.title: 2.6 Motion (all small-area, no full-screen redraw)
docs.text:
Motion Duration Easing What moves Selection bar to adjacent row 80 ms ease-out only the bar (lv_anim on y); text repaints two rows Selection bar jump > 3 rows / fast spin 0 ms — no anim; letter overlay shows instead Push screen (deeper) 120 ms ease-out-cubic list area slides in 24 px from the right, fades from 0; status bar title swaps instantly Pop screen (Menu) 100 ms ease-out-cubic list slides 24 px to the right and fades out Toast in / out 150 / 200 ms ease-out / ease-in one-row (30 / 45 px) strip slides down from under the status bar Volume HUD 120 ms in, hold 1200 ms, 200 ms out ease-out 26 px bottom strip; bar fill animates 60 ms Seek mode enter / leave 0 ms — colour swap only; haptic tick Progress bar 1 Hz step — invalidate only the bar rectangle Letter overlay appears instantly, fades 250 ms after the wheel stops ease-in 44 px tile + rail Cover Flow step 90 ms ease-out five tiles re-blit at new x/size; no rotation Power-hold progress linear over 2 s — 3 px line under the status bar grows left to right

Cap LVGL at 30 fps on the MCU (LV_DEF_REFR_PERIOD 33); 60 fps on the Y2 if the kernel gives a vsync'd fb.

docs.title: 3. Per-screen review and proposal
docs.text: Button conventions used throughout: Wheel scroll/adjust · Select open/choose · Menu back · Play/Pause global · ◁ ▷ prev/next (hold = seek) · Power hold 2 s lock, 10 s off.

docs.title: 3.1 Home
docs.text:
Current (home.png, home-clock.png, art-home.png): split list + right panel; the panel shows a generic disc glyph, "Nothing playing", "--:--" and a debug line "image 2.0 MB". When playing it shows art, file name and "⏸ Paused" but no progress. Status bar left slot is empty; battery reads "--".

Proposed (home-home, home-idle, home-home-dark):

  • Left 56 %: the seven items, chevrons on items that open a list, none on "Shuffle Songs". "Now Playing" greys out when nothing is queued instead of opening an empty screen.
  • Right panel, playing: art at panel width, title (Body, semibold) and artist (Small) centred, a 3 px progress bar, elapsed/remaining in Small. Paused shows the pause glyph in front of the elapsed time.
  • Right panel, idle: 48 px clock, date, one Small line "1,204 songs · 72 %". Remove "image 2.0 MB" from release builds (keep it behind a debug flag).
  • Status bar: clock in the left slot on Home only.

States: idle / playing / paused / library-not-built (panel shows "Update Library" prompt, Select on Music still works). Transitions: push on Select; the panel does not animate. Wheel: scroll items; Select opens; Play/Pause toggles playback without leaving Home.

docs.title: 3.2 Now Playing
docs.text:
Current (np-bt-badge.png, seek-scrub.png, np-bt-volume.png, art-cover.png, text-nowplaying.png): file name as title; format badge in blue sits where the artist should; "Playing – 1 of 3" is body-weight; the volume slider is as prominent as progress; seek mode recolours progress amber and adds a third "Seek 0:08" line with yet another bar; on BT the label changes to "Headset 47 %". Long titles clip (text-nowplaying.png).

Proposed (np-nowplaying, np-nowplaying-bt, np-seek, np-page2, np-volume-hud):

  • Status bar: left slot "3 of 12", centre "Now Playing", Bluetooth glyph in blue when streaming.
  • Art 112 / 168 px at the left; to its right the stack Title (Title size) → Artist (Body, ink2) → Album · Year (Small, ink3). Fall back to the file name only when there is no title tag, and then show the folder name as the "artist".
  • Pill row under the stack: format pill (accent_soft, e.g. "FLAC 16/44.1" or "AAC 44.1" when the BT codec is what's leaving the box) and output pill (outline: "Wired" or the headset's name). The output pill is where "Headset" belonged.
  • Progress: 4 px, elapsed left, remaining right, a quiet ink3 "repeat 1 / shuffle" word in the centre only when either is on.
  • Volume: bottom strip, label "Volume −18 dB" or "Headset 62 %" in Small, bar in ink2, 45 % of the width. On a volume change from any other screen the same strip appears as a HUD for 1.2 s (np-volume-hud).
  • Seek mode: the pill row is replaced by the seek time in Big amber; the progress bar grows to 6 px with a knob; hint line "Scroll: seek · Select: go · Menu: cancel". Leaving seek restores the pills. No third bar.
  • Page 2 (Select on Now Playing when not seeking): small art + title, star rating under it (wheel adjusts when focused), then Shuffle / Repeat / Gapless / Add to playlist / Go to album / Go to artist.

States: playing / paused (pause glyph before elapsed time, art unchanged) / seeking / BT link lost (toast, progress bar goes ink3, "Paused" under the title — see bt-dropped) / no art (placeholder tile with a ring, not a music-note glyph) / unsupported codec (toast "Can't play: AAC — skipped", auto-skip after 1.5 s). Transitions: push from a list = 120 ms slide; Menu returns to the list that queued the track. Wheel: volume; Select → page 2; hold Select → seek mode (wheel seeks, Select commits, Menu cancels); ◁ ▷ tracks, hold to scan at 4× with the seek bar shown.

docs.title: 3.3 Library (Artists, Albums, Songs, Genres, Compilations, Playlists, Album, Update Library)
docs.text:
Current (lib-songs.png, lib-album.png, lib-album-greyed.png, lib-artists.png, lib-building.png, lib-needs-writable.png, lib-cant-play.png, lib-update-done.png, music-empty.png): single-line rows with artist right-aligned (collides with long titles); album screen is a bare track list with no header; greyed unplayable rows give no reason until you press Select, then a yellow bar appears bottom-left; busy and error states are rendered as fake list rows ("Building library…" with dots as the first row, "Select to cancel" as the third); "No artists" is a selected blue row.

Proposed:

  • Songs / search results (lib-songs): two-line rows, title in Body and "Artist · Album" in Small ink2; 2 px scrollbar at the right edge; status-bar left slot shows the count.
  • Fast scroll (lib-songs-fastscroll): when wheel velocity passes the acceleration threshold, show a 44 px dark tile with the first letter of the focused row at the top-right and a 26-letter rail along the right edge with the current letter in ink at Small size, the rest at 8 px ink3 (every second letter on 320×240). The tile never covers the selection bar. Fade out 250 ms after the wheel stops. Sort keys ignore "The ", "A " and diacritics so the rail is useful.
  • Album (lib-album): header with 64 px art, album title (Title), "Artist · Year" (Body ink2), "3 songs · 9:41 · FLAC" (Small ink3); hairline; tracks as "n Title" with duration right. Unplayable tracks greyed with the codec in brackets ("Carrier Wave (AAC)") so the reason is visible before pressing.
  • Artists / Albums / Genres / Compilations: single-line rows with chevrons; show counts on the right ("4 albums") only on 480×360 where there is room.
  • Albums as Cover Flow (lib-coverflow): optional view toggled with ▷ on the Albums list. Five flat tiles: centre 96 px, neighbours 64 px, outer 48 px, no rotation or reflection; title and "Artist · Year · n songs" under the centre; status-bar left slot "7 of 31". Wheel moves one album per step; Play plays the album; Select opens it.
  • Playlists (lib-playlists): smart lists first (On-The-Go, Recently added, Most played, Unplayed) then .m3u files from the card, counts on the right.
  • Update Library / busy (lib-building): centred heading, determinate bar (songs found / total files from a first directory count), current folder in Small, hints "Menu: run in background · Select: cancel". While running in the background the status bar shows three busy dots in the left slot of every screen.
  • Empty and error states (lib-empty): heading in Title, one or two Small lines that say what to do, a single accent button. "Library needs a writable card" becomes a toast on the library root plus this empty state, never a selected list row.
  • Can't play: toast at the top in amber_soft with the codec and "skipped"; the track is skipped automatically after 1.5 s in a queue, or the row stays focused in a list.

Transitions: push/pop slides; Cover Flow step 90 ms. Wheel: as lists; in Cover Flow one album per detent with acceleration to 3 per detent.

docs.title: 3.4 Bluetooth
docs.text:
Current (bt-found.png, bt-pairing.png, bt-dropped.png, bt-forget-asks.png, settings-bt-streaming.png, bt-key-next.png): the settings page mixes status rows (Status, Address) with actions (Scan, Connect, Forget) in one list; the scan list shows a "Cancel pairing" row at the top and three-colour signal bars; "Headset disconnected" is a yellow band with "Reconnecting…" dots inline; "Forget" turns into "Select again" as a confirmation, which is easy to trigger by accident; the right pane in Settings dumps "SBC bitpool 53 · 328 kbit/s · 0 underruns" (fine for a dev build, not for users).

Proposed (bt-devices, bt-dropped):

  • One Devices screen: known devices first with their state on the right ("Connected" in on_accent on the selection bar, "Saved" in ink2), then found devices with signal bars (three bars, monochrome ink/line, no traffic-light colours), phones greyed and labelled "(phone)" because they cannot be sinks, then "Scan again". Scanning progress as four dots at the bottom in ink3.
  • Select on a saved device: Connect / Forget / Rename in a small list pushed from the right; Forget asks "Forget AirPods Pro?" with Select = yes, Menu = no — never a self-mutating row.
  • Pairing: the row's right text becomes "Pairing…" with three dots; Menu cancels (no "Cancel pairing" row).
  • Link lost: bt-dropped — toast "AirPods Pro disconnected · reconnecting…", playback paused, progress bar goes ink3, status-bar glyph grey. On success the toast becomes "AirPods Pro connected" in accent_soft for 1.2 s; on give-up, "Couldn't reconnect — playing on wired" or "— paused" if nothing is plugged in.
  • Codec detail stays in About › Diagnostics, not in the Settings right pane.
  • Status, Address and Audio output move to a short Bluetooth settings page: Bluetooth On/Off, Audio output Auto/Wired/Bluetooth, Devices ›, Absolute volume On/Off.

States: off / idle / scanning / pairing / connected / streaming / reconnecting / failed. Wheel: list; Select on a device = connect (found) or options (saved).

docs.title: 3.5 Settings
docs.text:
Current (settings.png, settings-bt.png, haptics, display): two-pane with values on the left rows and a centred prose summary on the right ("Resume playing / At power-up / On / Plays on power-up if it was playing") that reads as a paragraph; About shows "6 of 8 checks ok" and "nogit".

Proposed (settings-display):

  • Left list: Display, Click, Haptics, Gapless, Shuffle, Repeat, Resume, Bluetooth, About — values on the row where the value is a word, chevrons where it opens a page. Rows that toggle (Gapless, Resume) toggle on Select without leaving the list; a 60 ms value flip, haptic tick.
  • Right pane: a key/value summary left-aligned (Small), heading in Body semibold, one line of help in ink3. No centred prose.
  • Display page: Theme Light/Dark/Auto, Brightness, Dim after, Off after.
  • About: version, build, storage used/free, battery health, then Diagnostics › (checks, codec detail, underruns) and Licences › (settings-licences).

docs.title: 3.6 Files (Extras › Files)
docs.text:
Current (files.png, files-many.png, files-many-end.png, text-folder.png): fine functionally; the "… more (first 256 shown)" row is a blue selected row; the "F" letter tile sits over the list centre.

Proposed (files-browser): path in the status-bar left slot, folder/file glyphs from the icon set, size right-aligned in ink2, scrollbar. Folders with more than 256 entries show "256+" on the folder row and page in the list with "Load more" as the last row (not selected by default). Letter overlay as in the library (top-right tile).

docs.title: 3.7 Input widgets (text, password, number, slider, choice, date/time, search)
docs.text:
Current (in-text.png, wifi-kb.png, in-slider.png, in-choice.png, in-datetime.png): letters in an even row of five with the current one blue; hints as a sentence; no visible way to switch case/digits/symbols; slider is a bare bar; date/time fields underline the active field.

Proposed (in-text): field at the top in a surface box with a caret; a horizontal ring of nine glyphs with the current one in Big accent and widths proportional to glyph size; mode chips below (abc / ABC / 123 / #!? / space / ⌫) switched with ◁ ▷; hint line at the bottom. Password shows the typed glyph for 800 ms then a dot. Number/slider: value in Big centred, bar below, min/max in Small at the ends. Choice: plain list. Date/time: keep the field underline but make the active field accent and add the field name under it in Small.

Wheel: letters (acceleration jumps 3); Select types; Menu deletes (hold = clear); Play = done; ◁ ▷ = mode (text) or field (date/time).

docs.title: 3.8 Hold, lock and power
docs.text:
Current: nothing visible in the tours beyond the brief's description.

Proposed (hold-locked, hold-power-progress): while locked, any key press wakes the screen for 3 s and shows a dark pill at the bottom "Locked · hold Power 2 s to unlock"; the content behind is unchanged (no dim, so no full-screen blend). While Power is held, a 3 px accent line grows under the status bar over 2 s with a pill "Keep holding to lock · 10 s = off"; past 2 s the pill reads "Locked", the line resets and refills to 10 s in red with "Release to cancel · shutting down in 6"; haptic tick at 2 s and each second after 7 s.

On the product board the physical Hold switch drives the same pill without the progress line.

docs.title: 3.9 Splash and About
docs.text:
Current (splash.png): wordmark, a thin progress line, a row of eight boxed status glyphs with red crosses, a red "[1/2] battery: gauge: no response" line and the version.

Proposed: keep the wordmark and the progress line; move the self-test row to a debug splash (shown only when a check fails or when Menu is held at boot) and show it as a short list ("Battery gauge — no response") rather than crossed-out icons. Release splash: wordmark, progress line, version in ink3, 600 ms minimum.

Owner amendment, 2026-11-13: after testing on the Y2 the owner asked for the icon row back ("the device check screen has lost the icons and replaced with text - I want the icons back, that loading screen was good"). The release splash is now wordmark, progress line, icon row (Lucide icons, pulse / solid / red cross), version; the text list stays on the debug splash only.

docs.title: 3.10 Status bar (global)
docs.text: Left slot by screen: Home = clock · Now Playing = "n of m" · lists = count · Files = path · Album = album/artist name · Cover Flow = "n of m". Centre: screen title. Right: Bluetooth glyph (ink3 saved, ink connected, accent streaming), battery outline with fill (green while charging, red below 15 %) and the percentage as text only below 20 % or while charging. Three busy dots replace the left slot when the library is building in the background.

docs.title: 4. Mock-ups
docs.text:
All in mockups/, light theme unless named -dark, both 320x240 and 480x360:

File Section home-home, home-idle, home-home-dark 3.1 np-nowplaying, np-nowplaying-bt, np-nowplaying-dark, np-seek, np-page2, np-volume-hud 3.2 lib-songs, lib-songs-fastscroll, lib-album, lib-coverflow, lib-playlists, lib-building, lib-empty 3.3 bt-devices, bt-dropped 3.4 settings-display, settings-licences 3.5 files-browser 3.6 in-text 3.7 hold-locked, hold-power-progress 3.8

render.py regenerates them; every length comes from the metric table in §2.3, so it doubles as a layout reference.

docs.title: 5. Implementation notes (cost and cheaper alternatives)
docs.text:
Item Cost Cheaper alternative New Small font size (12 / 16 px) ~10 KB flash per profile Ship 12 px only; 480×360 uses 14 px Body in ink2 for secondary text Lucide icons, 14 glyphs × 2 sizes × 2 profiles, 1-bit alpha ~6 KB Render at 16 px only and let LVGL scale ×1.5 on 480×360 (slightly soft) 160×160 art thumbnails, LRU 24 1.2 MB PSRAM 96×96, LRU 6 (18 KB each) on the Pico 2 W; Now Playing at 1:1 Selection-bar slide (80 ms) invalidates two rows per frame Disable below 30 fps; the bar simply jumps Push/pop slide + fade list area redrawn ~4 frames Slide only (no alpha); or title-swap only on the Pico 2 W Toast / HUD strips one 22–26 px strip none needed — already minimal Letter overlay + rail 44 px tile + 26 small labels, drawn ~once per 100 ms Rail every second letter on 320×240 (as mocked) Cover Flow, five flat tiles five lv_image re-blits per step; no rotation Three tiles on the Pico 2 W Dark theme zero runtime cost; one token struct — Power-hold progress line 3 px × width invalidate at 10 Hz — Determinate library progress needs a first pass to count files (fast: directory entries only) Indeterminate bar that sweeps, still better than row-dots

Avoid: full-screen dim behind the lock pill (alpha blend of the whole frame), blur, gradients on backgrounds, animating the progress bar more often than 1 Hz, and per-frame redraw of the right pane on Home.

auto-skip with toast Library S 2 DS-5 LB-6 Cover Flow (flat five-tile) view on Albums Library M 2 NP-5 LB-7 Playlists screen (smart lists + .m3u) Library L 2 — BT-1 Devices screen (known / found / scan), signal bars monochrome Bluetooth M 3 DS-6 BT-2 Forget / pairing / reconnect flows with toasts; Suggested order: DS-1 → DS-2 → DS-3 → DS-4 → DS-5 (foundation, about a week), then NP-1 and LB-1/LB-2 (the two things users see most), then BT-1/BT-2, then the rest by impact.
